title.zh: 卷十八 列傳第八 趙倫之 蕭思話 臧燾
title.en: Volume 18 Biographies 8: Zhao Lunzhi, Xiao Sihua, Zang Dao
title.raw: 卷十八 列傳第八 趙倫之 蕭思話 臧燾 Volume 18 Biographies 8: Zhao Lunzhi, Xiao Sihua, Zang Dao

sentences.zh: 趙倫之蕭思話臧燾

translations.literal: Zhao Lunzhi, Xiao Sihua, Zang Dao
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Lunzhi, Xiao Sihua, and Zang Dao

sentences.zh: 赵伦之，字幼成，下邳僮人，宋孝穆皇后之弟也。

translations.literal: Zhao Lunzhi, styled Youcheng, was a man of Tong in Xiapi, younger brother of Empress Xiaomu of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Lunzhi, courtesy name Youcheng, came from Tong in Xiapi and was the younger brother of Empress Xiaomu of Song.

sentences.zh: 幼孤贫，事母以孝称。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he served his mother and was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Left fatherless in childhood and poor, he cared for his mother and won a reputation for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝起兵，以军功封阆中县五等侯，累迁雍州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song raised his army, Lunzhi was enfeoffed Marquis of the Fifth Rank of Langzhong county for military merit, and was promoted repeatedly to Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Wu of Song took up arms, Lunzhi earned the fifth-rank marquisate of Langzhong for battlefield service and rose step by step to governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 武帝北伐，倫之遣順陽太守傅弘之、扶風太守沈田子出嶢柳，大破姚泓于藍田。

translations.literal: On the Emperor's northern campaign, Lunzhi sent Shunyang Administrator Fu Hongzhi and Fufeng Administrator Shen Tianzi out through Yaoliu and routed Yao Hong at Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: During the emperor's northern expedition Lunzhi dispatched Shunyang administrator Fu Hongzhi and Fufeng administrator Shen Tianzi through Yaoliu and smashed Yao Hong at Lantian.

sentences.zh: 及武帝受命，以佐命功，封霄城縣侯。

translations.literal: When the Emperor received the Mandate, Lunzhi was enfeoffed Marquis of Xiaocheng county for merit in establishing the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor accepted Heaven's mandate, Lunzhi was made marquis of Xiaocheng for his part in founding the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 少帝即位，徵拜護軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shao succeeded, Lunzhi was summoned and appointed Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shao came to the throne, Lunzhi was called to court and made Protector of the Army.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三年，拜領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanjia he was appointed General-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanjia he received appointment as General-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 倫之雖外戚貴寵，而居身儉素，性野拙澀，於人間世事多所不解。

translations.literal: Though Lunzhi enjoyed the favor of an imperial in-law, he lived plainly and simply; coarse and awkward by nature, he understood little of worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Despite the privileges of an imperial connection, Lunzhi lived frugally; blunt and unpolished by temperament, he grasped little of everyday affairs.

sentences.zh: 久居方伯，公私富貴。

translations.literal: Long holding regional command, he grew rich in public and private means alike.
translations.idiomatic: After years as a regional commander he had amassed wealth both public and private.

sentences.zh: 入為護軍，資力不稱，以為見貶。

translations.literal: On entering office as Protector of the Army, his resources no longer matched his rank, and he took this as a slight.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to court as Protector of the Army his means no longer fit his station, and he felt himself demeaned.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫范泰好戲，笑謂曰：「司徒公缺，必用汝老奴。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Fan Tai loved jesting and laughed, saying to him, "When the post of Minister over the Masses falls vacant, they are sure to use you, old slave.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tai, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, loved to banter and told him with a laugh, "When the Ministry of Works opens up, they'll surely put you in it, old fellow.

sentences.zh: 我不言汝資地所任，要是外戚高秩次第所至耳。

translations.literal: I do not speak of the talent and standing fit for the office — it is simply the order in which imperial in-laws rise to high rank.
translations.idiomatic: I'm not talking about whether your talent suits the post — only that this is how high offices come to imperial relatives, one step after another.

sentences.zh: 」倫之大喜，每載酒肴詣泰。

translations.literal: " Lunzhi was greatly pleased and each time brought wine and food to Tai.
translations.idiomatic: " Lunzhi was delighted and thereafter often brought wine and dishes to Tai's house.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒，諡元侯。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died; posthumous title Marquis Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year and was posthumously titled Marquis Yuan.

sentences.zh: 子伯符嗣。

translations.literal: His son Bofu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bofu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 伯符字潤遠，少好弓馬，為甯遠將軍，總領義徒，以居宮城北。

translations.literal: Bofu, styled Runyuan, loved archery and horsemanship from youth; as General of Pacifying the Distance he commanded the righteous militia and was stationed north of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Bofu, courtesy name Runyuan, loved bow and horse from boyhood; as General of Pacifying the Distance he led the loyal militia and camped north of the palace.

sentences.zh: 每火起及有劫盜，輒身貫甲胄，助郡縣赴討，武帝甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Whenever fire broke out or bandits struck, he would don armor himself and help the commandery and counties in pursuit; the Emperor greatly praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever fire or robbery erupted he would arm himself and ride out with the local officials; the emperor greatly approved.

sentences.zh: 思話十許歲時，未知書，好騎屋棟，打細腰鼓，侵暴鄰曲，莫不患毒之。

translations.literal: When Sihua was about ten he did not yet know books; he loved riding house ridges, beating narrow-waisted drums, and bullying neighbors, who all hated and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: At about ten Sihua had not yet learned to read; he loved clambering along roof ridges, beating narrow-waisted drums, and terrorizing the neighborhood until everyone feared him.

sentences.zh: 自此折節，數年中遂有令譽。

translations.literal: From this he restrained himself, and within several years he had a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: After that he checked his ways, and within a few years had earned a good name.

sentences.zh: 頗工隸書，善彈琴，能騎射。

translations.literal: He was quite skilled at clerical script, good at the zither, and able in riding and shooting.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote clerical script well, played the zither, and was capable with bow and horse.

sentences.zh: 後襲爵封陽縣侯。

translations.literal: Later he inherited the title and was enfeoffed Marquis of Fengyang county.
translations.idiomatic: Later he inherited the marquisate of Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，為青州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era he served as Governor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanjia he governed Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 亡命司馬朗之兄弟聚党謀為亂，思話遣北海太守蕭汪之討斬之。

translations.literal: The outlaws Sima Langzhi and his brothers gathered a faction and plotted rebellion; Sihua sent Beihai Administrator Xiao Wangzhi to attack and behead them.
translations.idiomatic: Outlaw brothers Sima Langzhi and his kin raised a band to rebel; Sihua sent Beihai administrator Xiao Wangzhi to cut them down.

sentences.zh: 八年，魏軍大至，乃棄鎮奔平昌。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Wei armies came in force; he abandoned his post and fled to Pingchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Wei forces arrived in strength; he abandoned his command and fled to Pingchang.

sentences.zh: 魏軍定不至，由是征系尚方。

translations.literal: The Wei army in the end did not come; for this he was summoned and imprisoned in the Directorate of Palace Manufactories.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army never actually arrived, and for this he was summoned and held in the imperial workshops.

sentences.zh: 初在青州，常所用銅鬥覆在藥廚下，忽於鬥下得二死雀。

translations.literal: While earlier in Qing Province, a copper ladle-cover he always used lay under the medicine kitchen; suddenly beneath the ladle he found two dead sparrows.
translations.idiomatic: During his earlier tenure in Qing Province a copper ladle-cover he always used sat beneath the medicine kitchen, and one day he found two dead sparrows under it.

sentences.zh: 思話歎曰：「鬥覆而雙雀殞，其不祥乎？

translations.literal: Sihua sighed and said, "The ladle overturned and two sparrows perished — is this not ill omen?
translations.idiomatic: Sihua sighed and said, "The ladle overturned and two sparrows died — can this be anything but a bad sign?

sentences.zh: 」既而被系。

translations.literal: " Soon after he was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward he was taken into custody.

sentences.zh: 及梁州刺史甄法護在任失和，氐帥楊難當因此寇漢中，乃自徒中起思話為梁、南秦二州刺史，平漢中，悉收侵地，置戍葭萌水。

translations.literal: When Liang Province Inspector Zhen Fahu lost harmony in office and the Di chieftain Yang Nandang therefore raided Hanzhong, Sihua was raised from among the convicts to be Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin, pacified Hanzhong, recovered all seized territory, and set garrisons at Jiameng River.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang inspector Zhen Fahu's rule turned discordant and Di chieftain Yang Nandang raided Hanzhong, Sihua was pulled from the convict ranks to govern Liang and Southern Qin, recovered Hanzhong and all lost ground, and posted guards at Jiameng River.

sentences.zh: 思話遷鎮南鄭。

translations.literal: Sihua moved his headquarters to Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua transferred his headquarters to Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 法護，中山無極人也。

translations.literal: Fahu was a man of Wuji in Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Fahu came from Wuji in Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 過江，寓居南郡。

translations.literal: Crossing the river, he lodged in Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the Yangtze he lived in Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 弟法崇自少府為益州刺史。

translations.literal: His younger brother Fachong went from Director of the Palace Storehouse to Governor of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Fachong rose from director of the palace storehouse to governor of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 法護委鎮之罪，為府所收，於獄賜死。

translations.literal: For the crime of abandoning his post Fahu was taken by the provincial office and, in prison, was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Fahu was arrested for abandoning his post and, in prison, was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 文帝以法崇受任一方，命言法護病卒。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen, because Fachong held authority over a region, ordered it announced that Fahu had died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Since Fachong held a provincial command, Emperor Wen had it announced that Fahu had died of illness.

sentences.zh: 文帝使思話上定漢中本末，下之史官。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen had Sihua submit upstream the full account of pacifying Hanzhong and send it down to the historiographers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Sihua report upstream how Hanzhong had been settled and send the account to the historiographers.

sentences.zh: 十四年，遷臨川王義慶平西長史、南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Chief Administrator under Prince Linchuan Yiqing, Pacifier of the West, and Colonel of the Southern Man.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he became chief administrator to Prince Linchuan Yiqing as Pacifier of the West and Colonel of the Southern Man.

sentences.zh: 文帝賜以弓琴，手敕曰：「前得此琴，言是舊物，今以相借，並往桑弓一張，材理乃快。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen bestowed bow and zither on him with a personal edict saying, "I recently obtained this zither, said to be an old piece; I now lend it to you, and also send one mulberry bow — the wood and grain are excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen gave him a bow and zither with a personal note: "I lately acquired this zither, said to be an old instrument; I lend it to you now, and also send a mulberry bow whose wood and grain are fine.

sentences.zh: 良材美器，宜在盡用之地，丈人真無所與讓也。

translations.literal: Fine timber and fine instrument belong where they will be fully used; Elder, you truly need not decline.
translations.idiomatic: Good wood and a good instrument belong where they will be fully used; Elder, you need not refuse at all.

sentences.zh: 」嘗從文帝登鍾山北嶺，中道有磐石清泉，上使于石上彈琴，因賜以銀鍾酒，謂曰：「相賞有松石間意。

translations.literal: " Once he followed Emperor Wen up the northern ridge of Zhongshan; midway there was a boulder and clear spring; the Emperor had him play zither on the stone and then bestowed silver bell-wine, saying, "We share the mood of pines and stones.
translations.idiomatic: " Once he accompanied Emperor Wen to the north ridge of Zhongshan; halfway up there was a boulder and a clear spring; the emperor had him play on the stone and then gave silver bell-wine, saying, "We share the spirit of pines and stones.

sentences.zh: 」曆甯蠻校尉，雍州刺史，監四州軍事，徵為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: " He served successively as Colonel of Pacifying the Man, Governor of Yong, overseer of four provinces' military affairs, and was summoned as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: " He later served as Colonel of Pacifying the Man, governor of Yong, overseer of four provinces' military affairs, and was summoned to be Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 思話以去州無復事力，倩府軍身九人。

translations.literal: Sihua, leaving the province with no remaining staff, borrowed nine men from the princely household guard.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving his province without a retinue, Sihua borrowed nine men from the princely guard.

sentences.zh: 文帝戲之曰：「丈人終不為田父于閭里，何憂無人使邪？

translations.literal: Emperor Wen jested, "Elder, you will never become a village farmer in the lanes — why worry that no one will attend you?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen teased him: "Elder, you will never end up a village farmer in the lanes — why worry about having no attendants?

sentences.zh: 」未拜，遷護軍將軍。

translations.literal: " Before taking office he was transferred to General Who Protects the Army.
translations.idiomatic: " Before he could take up the post he was moved to General Who Protects the Army.

sentences.zh: 是時，魏攻懸瓠，文帝將大舉北侵，朝士僉同，思話固諫不從。

translations.literal: At that time Wei attacked Xuanyong; Emperor Wen planned a great northern invasion; court officials all agreed, but Sihua firmly remonstrated and was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei attacked Xuanyong the emperor planned a major northern campaign; the court was unanimous, but Sihua argued hard against it and was overruled.

sentences.zh: 魏軍退，即代孝武為徐、兗二州刺史，監四州軍事。

translations.literal: When the Wei army withdrew, he immediately replaced Xiaowu as Governor of Xu and Yan and overseer of four provinces' military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wei army withdrew he at once replaced Xiaowu as governor of Xu and Yan and overseer of four provinces' military affairs.

sentences.zh: 後為圍碻磝城不拔，退師曆下，為江夏王義恭所奏免官。

translations.literal: Later, besieging the fortress of Queqi without taking it, he withdrew the army below Li and was impeached and removed from office by Prince Jiangxia Yigong.
translations.idiomatic: Later, failing to take Queqi fortress, he withdrew below Li and was impeached and dismissed by Prince Jiangxia Yigong.

sentences.zh: 所至雖無皎皎清節，亦無穢黷之累。

translations.literal: Wherever he served, though he had no dazzling purity of conduct, he also had no stain of corruption.
translations.idiomatic: In every post, though he showed no blazing integrity, he bore no taint of corruption either.

sentences.zh: 愛才好士，人多歸之。

translations.literal: He loved talent and honored scholars; many men rallied to him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved talent and honored scholars, and many men gathered to him.

sentences.zh: 長子惠開少有風氣，涉獵文史，家雖貴戚而居服簡素。

translations.literal: His eldest son Huikai in youth had spirit; he ranged through literature and history, and though the family was an honored in-law clan he lived in plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Huikai had spirit even as a youth; he read widely in letters and history, and though born to an imperial connection he dressed and lived simply.

sentences.zh: 初為秘書郎，意趣與人多不同，比肩或三年不共語。

translations.literal: At first he was a Secretary Gentleman; his interests differed greatly from others', and some colleagues went three years without speaking to him.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as a secretary gentleman; his temperament set him apart, and some colleagues went three years without exchanging a word with him.

sentences.zh: 外祖光祿大夫沛郡劉成戒之曰：「汝恩戚家子，無多異以取天下之疾。

translations.literal: His maternal grandfather, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Liu Cheng of Pei Commandery, admonished him, "You are a son of an in-law house — do not make yourself so odd as to draw the world's dislike.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal grandfather Liu Cheng, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of Pei, warned him, "You are from an in-law house — do not make yourself so strange that the world turns against you.

sentences.zh: 」轉太子舍人，與汝南周朗同官友善，以偏奇相尚。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Attendant of the Heir Apparent; he and Zhou Lang of Runan held the same office and were friendly, each prizing the other's eccentric brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: " He became attendant to the heir apparent; he and Zhou Lang of Runan served together, became friends, and admired each other's eccentric brilliance.

sentences.zh: 孝建元年，為黃門侍郎，與侍中何偃爭推積射將軍徐沖之事，偃任遇甚隆，怒使門下推彈惠開，乃上表解職，由此忤旨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaojian he was Gentleman at the Yellow Gate; he disputed with Attendant-in-Ordinary He Yan over promoting General of Accumulated Shots Xu Chong; Yan's favor was very high and in anger he had the Secretariat impeach Huikai; Huikai submitted a memorial resigning, and by this offended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiaojian he was a gentleman at the Yellow Gate and clashed with attendant He Yan over promoting General of Accumulated Shots Xu Chong; Yan's influence was great and he had the secretariat impeach Huikai, who submitted his resignation and thereby offended the throne.

sentences.zh: 別敕有司以屬疾多，免之。

translations.literal: A separate edict ordered the offices, on grounds of frequent illness, to dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: A separate edict ordered the offices to dismiss him on grounds of frequent illness.

sentences.zh: 思話素恭謹，與惠開不同，每加嫌責；

translations.literal: Sihua had always been respectful and cautious, unlike Huikai, and always added blame and reproof;
translations.idiomatic: Sihua had always been respectful and cautious, unlike Huikai, and constantly reproved him;

sentences.zh: 及見惠開自解表，歎曰：「兒不幸與周朗周旋，理應如此。

translations.literal: when he saw Huikai's memorial of self-dismissal he sighed and said, "The boy was unfortunate to keep company with Zhou Lang — it had to come to this.
translations.idiomatic: when he saw Huikai's resignation memorial he sighed and said, "The boy was unlucky to keep company with Zhou Lang — it had to end this way.

sentences.zh: 」杖之二百。

translations.literal: " He had him beaten two hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: " He had him beaten two hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 尋除中庶子，丁父艱，居喪有孝性。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Junior Mentor; on his father's death he observed mourning with filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was made junior mentor; when his father died he mourned with genuine filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 家素事佛，凡為父起四寺：南岡下名曰禪岡寺，曲阿舊鄉宅名曰禪鄉寺，京口墓亭名曰禪亭寺，所封封陽縣名曰禪封寺。

translations.literal: The family had long honored Buddhism; for his father he built four temples: below the southern ridge, named Chan Ridge Temple; at the old home in Qu'e, named Chan Village Temple; at the tomb pavilion in Jingkou, named Chan Pavilion Temple; in his enfeoffed Fengyang county, named Chan Feng Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The family had long been Buddhist; for his father he raised four temples: Chan Ridge below the southern hill, Chan Village at the old home in Qu'e, Chan Pavilion at the tomb pavilion in Jingkou, and Chan Feng in his fief of Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 謂國僚曰：「封秩鮮而兄弟甚多，若全關一人，則在我所讓，若人人等分，又事可悲恥。

translations.literal: He told the state staff, "The fief income is small and the brothers are many; if one alone received the whole grant it would be my own surrender, but equal shares for all would be a shameful affair.
translations.idiomatic: He told the staff, "The fief income is small and the brothers are many; if one man took the whole grant it would be my own surrender, but equal shares for all would be shameful.

sentences.zh: 寺眾既立，自宜悉供僧眾。

translations.literal: Since the temple communities are established, they should all supply the monastic assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the temple communities exist, they should all support the monks.

sentences.zh: 」襲封封陽縣侯，為新安王子鸞冠軍長史。

translations.literal: " He inherited the marquisate of Fengyang and served as Chief Administrator to Prince Xin'an Ziluan, Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: " He inherited Fengyang and served as chief administrator to Prince Xin'an Ziluan, Champion General.

sentences.zh: 惠開妹當適桂陽王休範，女又當適孝武子，發遣之資，應須二千萬。

translations.literal: Huikai's sister was to marry Prince Guiyang Xiufan and his daughter was to marry Emperor Xiaowu's son; the expenses of sending them off would require twenty million.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai's sister was to marry Prince Guiyang Xiufan and his daughter Emperor Xiaowu's son; sending them off would cost some twenty million.

sentences.zh: 乃以為豫章內史，聽其肆意聚納，由是在郡著貪暴之聲。

translations.literal: He was therefore made Interior Minister of Yuzhang and allowed to gather and extort at will; for this in the commandery he gained a reputation for greed and cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore made interior minister of Yuzhang and allowed to squeeze what he could; in the commandery he earned a name for greed and brutality.

sentences.zh: 再遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 孝武與劉秀之詔曰：「今以蕭惠開為憲司，冀當稱職。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu wrote to Liu Xiuzhi, "I now appoint Xiao Huikai to the censorate, hoping he will prove fit for the office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu wrote Liu Xiuzhi, "I now appoint Xiao Huikai to the censorate, hoping he will prove equal to the post.

sentences.zh: 但一往眼額，已自殊有所震。

translations.literal: But at first sight his brow and eyes already inspire a special dread.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at first sight his brow and eyes already strike a special fear.

sentences.zh: 」及在職，百僚憚之。

translations.literal: " Once in office, the hundred officials feared him.
translations.idiomatic: " Once in office, the hundred officials feared him.

sentences.zh: 後拜益州刺史，路經江陵。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Yi Province and passed through Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed governor of Yi Province and passed through Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 時吉翰子在荊州，共惠開有舊，為設女樂。

translations.literal: At that time Ji Han's son was in Jing Province; he and Huikai had old ties and set out female musicians for him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Han's son was then in Jing Province; he and Huikai were old acquaintances and provided female musicians.

sentences.zh: 樂人有美者，惠開就求不得，又欲以四女妓易之，不許。

translations.literal: Among the musicians was a beautiful one; Huikai asked for her and was refused; he also wished to exchange four female performers for her and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: One musician was beautiful; Huikai asked for her and was refused, then tried to trade four female performers for her and was denied again.

sentences.zh: 惠開怒，收吉斬之，即納其妓。

translations.literal: Huikai in anger seized Ji and beheaded him, then took the performers for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai in rage seized Ji, had him beheaded, and took the performers.

sentences.zh: 啟云：「吉為劉義宣所遇，交結不逞，向臣訕毀朝政，輒已戮之。

translations.literal: He reported, "Ji had been favored by Liu Yixuan and consorted with the unruly; he slandered the court to me, and I have already executed him.
translations.idiomatic: He reported, "Ji had been favored by Liu Yixuan and kept company with the unruly; he slandered the court to me, and I have already killed him.

sentences.zh: 」孝武稱快。

translations.literal: " Emperor Xiaowu expressed satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xiaowu declared himself pleased.

sentences.zh: 惠開素有大志，至蜀欲廣樹經略。

translations.literal: Huikai had long harbored great ambition; reaching Shu he wished to expand strategy on every side.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai had long nursed grand ambitions; reaching Shu he meant to extend strategy on every front.

sentences.zh: 善於敘述，聞其言者皆以為大功可立。

translations.literal: Skilled in narration, all who heard him thought great achievement could be established.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke with force, and all who heard him believed great deeds lay within reach.

sentences.zh: 才疏意廣，竟無成功。

translations.literal: Talent was thin and intent broad; in the end nothing succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His talent was narrow and his designs vast; in the end nothing came of them.

sentences.zh: 嚴用威刑，蜀人號曰：「臥虎」。

translations.literal: He used harsh punishments strictly; the people of Shu called him "Crouching Tiger."
translations.idiomatic: He ruled with harsh punishments; the people of Shu called him the Crouching Tiger.

sentences.zh: 明識過人，嘗供三千沙門，一閱其名，退無所失。

translations.literal: His discernment surpassed others; once he feasted three thousand monks and, having read their names once, afterward forgot none.
translations.idiomatic: His memory was extraordinary; once he feasted three thousand monks, read their names once, and afterward forgot none.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，晉安王子勳反，惠開乃集將佐謂曰：「吾荷世祖之眷，當投袂萬里，推奉九江。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming succeeded, Prince Jin'an Zixun rebelled; Huikai gathered his staff and said, "I bear Emperor Shizu's favor and ought to shake out my sleeves for ten thousand li and uphold Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming succeeded, Prince Jin'an Zixun rebelled; Huikai gathered his staff and said, "I owe Emperor Shizu's favor and should march ten thousand li to uphold Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 」蜀人素怨惠開嚴，及是所遣兵皆不得前。

translations.literal: The people of Shu had long resented Huikai's severity, and now the troops he sent could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu had long resented his severity, and now the troops he sent could not move.

sentences.zh: 晉原郡反，諸郡悉應，並來圍城。

translations.literal: Jinyuan Commandery rebelled and all commanderies responded, coming together to besiege the city.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyuan commandery rose and the rest followed, converging to besiege the city.

sentences.zh: 城內東兵不過二千，凡蜀人，惠開疑之，悉皆遣出。

translations.literal: Inside the city the eastern troops numbered no more than two thousand; all were men of Shu whom Huikai suspected, and he sent them all out.
translations.idiomatic: Within the walls the eastern troops numbered barely two thousand; all were Shu men whom Huikai distrusted, and he expelled them.

sentences.zh: 子勳尋敗，蜀人並欲屠城，以望厚賞。

translations.literal: When Zixun was soon defeated, the people of Shu all wished to slaughter the city for rich reward.
translations.idiomatic: When Zixun was soon defeated, the Shu people all wanted to sack the city for rich reward.

sentences.zh: 明帝以蜀土險遠，赦其誅責，遣其弟惠基使蜀宣旨。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming, because Shu was rugged and remote, pardoned the capital offense and sent Huikai's younger brother Huiji to Shu to proclaim the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shu was rugged and remote, Emperor Ming pardoned the death sentence and sent Huikai's younger brother Huiji to proclaim the edict.

sentences.zh: 而蜀人志在屠城，不使王命速達，遏留惠基。

translations.literal: But the Shu people intended to slaughter the city and would not let the imperial command arrive quickly; they detained Huiji.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu people meant to slaughter the city and would not let the imperial command through quickly; they detained Huiji.

sentences.zh: 惠基破其渠帥，然後得前。

translations.literal: Huiji broke their chieftains and then was able to proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Huiji broke their chieftains and only then could advance.

sentences.zh: 惠開奉旨歸順，城圍得解。

translations.literal: Huikai received the edict and submitted; the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai accepted the edict and submitted, and the siege was lifted.

sentences.zh: 明帝又遣惠開宗人寶首水路慰勞益州，寶首欲以平蜀為功，更獎說蜀人，處處蜂起。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming also sent Huikai's clansman Baoshou by water route to comfort and reward Yi Province; Baoshou wished to make pacifying Shu his achievement and again incited the Shu people, who rose everywhere like hornets.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming also sent his clansman Baoshou by water to comfort Yi Province; Baoshou hoped to win credit by pacifying Shu and again stirred the Shu people until they rose everywhere.

sentences.zh: 惠開乃啟陳情事，遣宋甯太守蕭惠訓、州別駕費欣業分兵並進，大破之，禽寶首送之。

translations.literal: Huikai then memorialized the full circumstances and sent Songning Administrator Xiao Huixun and Provincial Assistant Fei Xinye with divided forces advancing together; they routed them greatly, captured Baoshou and sent him in.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai then memorialized the facts and sent Songning administrator Xiao Huixun and provincial assistant Fei Xinye with divided forces; they won a great victory, seized Baoshou, and sent him in.

sentences.zh: 惠開至都，明帝問其故，侍衛左右莫不悚然側目，惠開舉動自若，從容答曰：「臣唯知逆順，不識天命。

translations.literal: When Huikai reached the capital, Emperor Ming asked the reason; attendants and guards all stared in dread, but Huikai's bearing was as usual; calmly he answered, "Your servant knows only loyalty and rebellion, not Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: When Huikai reached the capital the emperor asked why; attendants stared in dread, but Huikai was unmoved and answered calmly, "I know only loyalty and rebellion, not Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「非臣不亂，非臣不平。」

translations.literal: " He also said, "Had I not been here, there would have been chaos; had I not been here, there would have been no peace."
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "Without me there would have been chaos; without me there would have been no peace."

sentences.zh: 初，惠開府錄事參軍劉希微負蜀人責將百萬，為責主所制，未得俱還。

translations.literal: Earlier, Huikai's staff recorder Liu Xiwai owed the people of Shu nearly a million in debt; held by creditors, he could not return together.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier his staff recorder Liu Xiwai owed the people of Shu nearly a million and was held by creditors, unable to leave with the rest.

sentences.zh: 惠開與希微共事不厚，而廄中凡有馬六十匹，悉以乞希微償責。

translations.literal: Huikai had not been close to Xiwai in service, yet of the sixty horses in the stables he gave them all to Xiwai to pay the debt.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai had not been close to Xiwai, yet gave him all sixty horses in the stables to settle the debt.

sentences.zh: 其意趣不常如是。

translations.literal: His bent of mind was not always like this.
translations.idiomatic: His temperament was not always so.

sentences.zh: 惠開還資二千餘萬，悉散施道俗，一無所留。

translations.literal: Huikai returned with more than twenty million in assets and distributed it all to monks and laymen, keeping nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai returned with more than twenty million in assets and gave it all to monks and lay believers, keeping nothing.

sentences.zh: 後除桂陽王休範征北長史、南東海太守。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Chief Administrator to Prince Guiyang Xiufan, Pacifier of the North, and Administrator of Eastern Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made chief administrator to Prince Guiyang Xiufan as Pacifier of the North and administrator of Eastern Sea.

sentences.zh: 其年，會稽太守蔡興宗之郡，惠開自京口請假還都，相逢于曲阿。

translations.literal: That year, when Kuaiji Administrator Cai Xingzong went to his commandery, Huikai took leave from Jingkou to return to the capital and met him at Qu'e.
translations.idiomatic: That year, as Kuaiji administrator Cai Xingzong went to his post, Huikai took leave from Jingkou to return to the capital and met him at Qu'e.

sentences.zh: 惠開先與興宗名位略同，又經情款，自以負釁摧屈，慮興宗不能詣己，戒勒部下：蔡會稽部伍若問，慎不得答。

translations.literal: Huikai and Xingzong had once been roughly equal in name and rank and had been on friendly terms; he felt himself disgraced and humbled by guilt and feared Xingzong would not visit him, so he ordered his staff: if asked about Administrator Cai of Kuaiji, they must not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai and Xingzong had once been equals in rank and on friendly terms; now, burdened with guilt and humbled, he feared Xingzong would not call on him and ordered his staff: if anyone asked about the Kuaiji administrator, they were not to answer.

sentences.zh: 惠開素嚴，部下莫敢違。

translations.literal: Huikai had always been strict; his subordinates dared not disobey.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai had always ruled sternly, and his men dared not disobey.

sentences.zh: 興宗見惠開舟力甚盛，遣人訪訊，事力二三百人皆低頭直去，無一人答者。

translations.literal: Xingzong saw Huikai's boat escort was very grand; he sent men to inquire, and two or three hundred attendants all lowered their heads and walked straight on — not one answered.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong saw Huikai's escort was very grand and sent men to inquire; two or three hundred attendants lowered their heads and passed on without a single reply.

sentences.zh: 尋除少府，加給事中。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Director of the Palace Storehouse and added Supervising Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was made director of the palace storehouse with the added title Supervising Master of Writing.

sentences.zh: 惠開素剛，至是益不得志，曰：「大丈夫入管喉舌，出蒞方伯，乃復低頭入中邪。

translations.literal: Huikai had always been stiff by nature; now he was even more frustrated and said, "A great man enters to manage the throat and tongue, goes out to govern a region — and must he again bow his head and enter the inner offices?
translations.idiomatic: Huikai had always been proud; now he was still more frustrated and said, "A great man enters to govern the tongue of the state and goes out to command a province — must he bow his head and enter the inner offices again?

sentences.zh: 」寺內所住齋前，向種花草甚美，惠開悉剷除別種白楊。

translations.literal: Before the quarters where he lived in the directorate there had been lovely flowers and grasses planted; Huikai uprooted them all and planted white poplars instead.
translations.idiomatic: Before his quarters in the directorate lovely flowers had been planted; Huikai uprooted them and planted white poplars instead.

sentences.zh: 每謂人曰：「人生不得行胸懷，雖壽百歲猶為夭也。

translations.literal: He often told people, "If a man cannot act out what is in his breast, though he lives a hundred years it is still an early death.
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "If a man cannot live out what is in his heart, even a hundred years is an early death.

sentences.zh: 」發病嘔血，吐物如肝肺者。

translations.literal: He fell ill, vomited blood, and brought up matter like liver and lungs.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill, vomited blood, and brought up matter like liver and lung.

sentences.zh: 卒，子睿嗣，齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: He died; his son Rui succeeded; when Qi received the Mandate the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Rui succeeded; when Qi took the throne the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 惠開與諸弟並不睦，惠基使至益州，遂不相見。

translations.literal: Huikai was not on good terms with any of his brothers; when Huiji was sent to Yi Province they did not meet at all.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai was at odds with all his brothers; when Huiji was sent to Yi Province they never met.

sentences.zh: 與同產弟惠明亦致嫌隙云。

translations.literal: With his full brother Huiming he also came to estrangement.
translations.idiomatic: With his full brother Huiming he also fell into estrangement.

sentences.zh: 惠明其次弟也，亦有時譽。

translations.literal: Huiming was the next younger brother and also had a reputation in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Huiming, the next younger brother, also had a reputation in his day.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，為吳興太守，郡界有卞山，山下有項羽廟。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he was Administrator of Wuxing; within the commandery was Mount Bian, below which stood a temple to Xiang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Taishi he governed Wuxing; in the commandery stood Mount Bian with a temple to Xiang Yu below it.

sentences.zh: 相承雲羽多居郡聽事，前後太守不敢上。

translations.literal: Tradition held that Yu often occupied the commandery hall; successive administrators dared not ascend it.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition held that Yu often occupied the commandery hall, and successive administrators dared not enter it.

sentences.zh: 惠明謂綱紀曰：「孔季恭嘗為此郡，未聞有災。

translations.literal: Huiming told the clerks, "Kong Jigong once held this commandery and no disaster was heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Huiming told the clerks, "Kong Jigong once governed here and no disaster followed.

sentences.zh: 」遂盛設筵榻接賓，數日，見一人長丈餘，張弓挾矢向惠明，既而不見。

translations.literal: He then set out a full banquet and received guests; after several days he saw a man more than ten feet tall, drawing a bow and nocking an arrow toward Huiming, then vanishing.
translations.idiomatic: He then held a full banquet and received guests; after several days a man more than ten feet tall appeared, drew a bow and aimed at Huiming, then vanished.

sentences.zh: 因發背，旬日而卒。

translations.literal: Back pain then broke out; within ten days he died.
translations.idiomatic: Pain then seized his back; within ten days he was dead.

sentences.zh: 子視素，梁天監中，位丹陽尹丞。

translations.literal: His son Shisu, in the Tianjian era of Liang, held the post of Assistant Magistrate of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shisu, under Liang in the Tianjian era, served as assistant magistrate of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 初拜日，武帝賜錢八萬，視素一朝散之親友。

translations.literal: On the day of his first appointment Emperor Wu bestowed eighty thousand cash; Shisu distributed it in one morning to friends and kin.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his first appointment Emperor Wu gave him eighty thousand cash, which Shisu gave away in one morning to friends and kin.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒左西屬、南徐州中從事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Western Attendant of the Minister of Masses and Middle Aide of Southern Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to western attendant of the Minister of Masses and middle aide of Southern Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 性靜退，少嗜欲，好學，能清言，榮利不關於中，喜怒不形於色。

translations.literal: By nature quiet and retiring, with few desires from youth, he loved learning, could speak with clarity, cared nothing for profit and honor in his heart, and did not show joy or anger on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet and retiring by nature, with few desires from youth, he loved learning, spoke with clarity, cared nothing for profit or honor, and showed neither joy nor anger on his face.

sentences.zh: 在人間及居職，並任情通率，不自矜尚，天然簡素。

translations.literal: Among men and in office he was always spontaneous and open, never self-admiring, naturally plain.
translations.idiomatic: In society and in office he was always spontaneous and open, never self-admiring, naturally plain.

sentences.zh: 及在京口，便有終焉之志。

translations.literal: While at Jingkou he already had the will to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: While at Jingkou he already meant to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 後為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he served as Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as gentleman of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 在位少時，求為諸暨令。

translations.literal: After a short time in office he requested to be Magistrate of Zhuji.
translations.idiomatic: After a brief tenure he asked to be magistrate of Zhuji.

sentences.zh: 到縣十餘日，掛衣冠於縣門而去。

translations.literal: Within ten-odd days of reaching the county he hung his cap and robe at the county gate and left.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days of reaching the county he hung his cap and robe at the gate and departed.

sentences.zh: 獨居屏事，非親戚不得至其籬門。

translations.literal: He lived alone behind closed doors; except for kin none could reach his hedge gate.
translations.idiomatic: He lived alone behind closed doors; except for kin none could reach his gate.

sentences.zh: 妻即齊太尉王儉女，久與別居，遂無子。

translations.literal: His wife was the daughter of Grand Commandant Wang Jian of Qi; long separated from him, she bore no sons.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was Grand Commandant Wang Jian's daughter of Qi; long separated from him, she bore no sons.

sentences.zh: 卒，親故跡其事行，諡曰貞文先生。

translations.literal: When he died, friends and kin traced his conduct and posthumous title was given: Master Zhenwen.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, friends and kin recorded his conduct and he was posthumously titled Master Zhenwen.

sentences.zh: 惠明弟惠基，幼以外戚見宋江夏王義恭，歎其詳審，以女結婚。

translations.literal: Huiming's younger brother Huiji in youth was seen by Prince Jiangxia Yiqing of Song as an imperial in-law; Yiqing admired his thoroughness and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Huiming's younger brother Huiji, seen in youth by Prince Jiangxia Yiqing as an imperial connection, impressed Yiqing with his thoroughness and received his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 曆中書黃門郎。

translations.literal: He served successively as Gentleman of the Secretariat and at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively at the secretariat and the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 惠基善隸書及弈棋，齊高帝與之情好相得。

translations.literal: Huiji was skilled at clerical script and weiqi; Emperor Gao of Qi was on close friendly terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: Huiji wrote clerical script and played weiqi well; Emperor Gao of Qi was on close terms with him.

sentences.zh: 桂陽王休范妃，惠基姊也，高帝謂之曰：「卿家桂陽，遂復作賊。

translations.literal: The consort of Prince Guiyang Xiufan was Huiji's elder sister; the Emperor said to him, "Your family's Prince Guiyang has again turned rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Guiyang Xiufan's consort was Huiji's elder sister; the emperor told him, "Your family's Prince Guiyang has turned rebel again.

sentences.zh: 」高帝頓新亭壘，以惠基為軍副。

translations.literal: When the Emperor halted at Xinting rampart he made Huiji deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor halted at Xinting rampart he made Huiji deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 惠基弟惠朗親為休范攻戰，惠基在城內了不自疑。

translations.literal: Huiji's younger brother Huilang personally fought for Xiufan in attack; Huiji inside the city was not the least suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Huiji's younger brother Huilang fought for Xiufan in person; Huiji inside the city showed not the slightest doubt.

sentences.zh: 後為長兼侍中。

translations.literal: Later he served as Concurrent Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as concurrent attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 袁粲、劉彥節起兵之夕，高帝以彥節是惠基妹夫，惠基時直在省，遣王敬則觀其指趣，見惠基安靜，不與彥節相知，由是益加恩信。

translations.literal: On the night Yuan Tan and Liu Yanjie raised troops, the Emperor, because Yanjie was Huiji's brother-in-law and Huiji was then on duty in the palace, sent Wang Jingze to observe his intent; seeing Huiji calm and unconnected with Yanjie, he therefore added favor and trust.
translations.idiomatic: On the night Yuan Tan and Liu Yanjie rose, the emperor, knowing Yanjie was Huiji's brother-in-law and Huiji was on palace duty, sent Wang Jingze to watch him; finding Huiji calm and unconnected with Yanjie, he trusted him all the more.

sentences.zh: 仕齊為都官尚書，掌吏部。

translations.literal: Serving Qi he was Minister of Justice and controlled the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he was minister of justice and controlled the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 永明中為侍中，領驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era he was Attendant-in-Ordinary and commanded the Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming he was attendant-in-ordinary and commanded the Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 尚書令王儉朝宗貴望，惠基同在禮閣，非公事不私覿焉。

translations.literal: Wang Jian, Minister of Writing, was the court's honored hope; Huiji was with him in the Ritual Office and except for public business did not visit him privately.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Writing Wang Jian was the court's great hope; Huiji served with him in the Ritual Office and except on public business never visited him privately.

sentences.zh: 遷太常，加給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master of Ceremonies and added Supervising Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to grand master of ceremonies with the added title Supervising Master of Writing.

sentences.zh: 自宋大明以來，聲伎所尚，多鄭、衛，而雅樂正聲鮮有好者。

translations.literal: From the Daming era of Song onward, what music and performers favored was mostly Zheng and Wei; few loved the orthodox music and correct tones.
translations.idiomatic: From Song's Daming era onward popular music favored Zheng and Wei styles; few cared for orthodox tones.

sentences.zh: 惠基解音律，尤好魏三祖曲及相和歌，每奏輒賞悅不能已。

translations.literal: Huiji understood music and especially loved the Three Ancestors' tunes of Wei and the harmonized songs; whenever they were played he was delighted beyond stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Huiji understood music and especially loved Wei's Three Ancestors tunes and harmonized songs; whenever they were played he could not contain his delight.

sentences.zh: 當時能棋人琅邪王抗第一品，吳郡褚思莊、會稽夏赤松第二品。

translations.literal: At that time the best weiqi players were Wang Kang of Langye, first rank, and Chu Sizhuang of Wu and Xia Chisong of Kuaiji, second rank.
translations.idiomatic: The best weiqi players then were Wang Kang of Langye, first rank, and Chu Sizhuang of Wu and Xia Chisong of Kuaiji, second rank.

sentences.zh: 赤松思速，善於大行，思莊戲遲，巧於鬥棋。

translations.literal: Chisong was quick in thought and good at large formations; Sizhuang was slow in play and clever in close combat.
translations.idiomatic: Chisong thought quickly and excelled at large formations; Sizhuang played slowly and was clever in close combat.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝時，羊玄保為會稽，帝遣思莊入東，與玄保戲，因置局圖，還於帝前覆之。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wen's time Yang Xuanbao was in Kuaiji; the Emperor sent Sizhuang east to play with Xuanbao, had a board diagram made, and on return covered it before the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen, Yang Xuanbao governed Kuaiji; the emperor sent Sizhuang east to play him, had the board diagram recorded, and on return covered it before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝使思莊與王抗交賭，自食時至日暮，一局始竟。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao of Qi had Sizhuang play a matched game with Wang Kang from mealtime until dusk before one game ended.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao of Qi had Sizhuang play Wang Kang for stakes from mealtime until dusk before one game ended.

sentences.zh: 上倦，遣還省，至五更方決。

translations.literal: The Emperor grew weary and sent him back to his office; the outcome was decided only at the fifth watch.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew weary and sent him back to his office; the outcome was settled only at the fifth watch.

sentences.zh: 抗睡於局後寢，思莊達旦不寐。

translations.literal: Kang slept on the board behind the game; Sizhuang stayed awake until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Kang slept behind the board; Sizhuang stayed awake until dawn.

sentences.zh: 時或云，思莊所以品第致高，緣其用思深久，人不能對。

translations.literal: Some then said Sizhuang's high ranking came because his thinking ran deep and long and others could not answer him.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Sizhuang's high rank came because he thought long and deeply and others could not match him.

sentences.zh: 抗、思莊並至給事中。

translations.literal: Kang and Sizhuang both reached Supervising Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Kang and Sizhuang both rose to Supervising Master of Writing.

sentences.zh: 永明中，敕使抗品棋，竟陵王子良使惠基掌其事。

translations.literal: In Yongming an edict had Kang rank weiqi players; Prince Jingling Ziliang had Huiji manage the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming an edict had Kang rank weiqi players; Prince Jingling Ziliang had Huiji oversee it.

sentences.zh: 初，思話先于曲阿起宅，有閑曠之致。

translations.literal: Earlier Sihua had first built a residence at Qu'e with an air of open spaciousness.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Sihua had built a residence at Qu'e with an air of open spaciousness.

sentences.zh: 惠基常謂所親曰：「須婚嫁畢，當歸老舊廬。

translations.literal: Huiji often told those close to him, "When the marriages are finished I shall return to my old lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Huiji often told intimates, "When the marriages are done I shall return to the old lodge.

sentences.zh: 」立身退素，朝廷稱為善士。

translations.literal: His conduct was retiring and plain; the court called him a good man.
translations.idiomatic: Retiring and plain in conduct, the court called him a good man.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously given Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously given Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 子洽字宏稱。

translations.literal: His son Qia, styled Hongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qia, courtesy name Hongcheng.

sentences.zh: 幼敏寤，年七歲，誦楚辭略上口。

translations.literal: Clever and quick from infancy, at seven he could recite most of the Songs of Chu from memory.
translations.idiomatic: Clever from infancy, at seven he could recite most of the Songs of Chu from memory.

sentences.zh: 及長，好學博涉，善屬文。

translations.literal: When grown he loved learning and ranged widely; he was skilled at writing.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he loved learning, read widely, and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 仕梁位南徐州中從事。

translations.literal: Serving Liang he held the post of Middle Aide of Southern Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he served as middle aide of Southern Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 近畿重鎮，職吏數千人，前後居者皆致巨富。

translations.literal: A key town near the capital, its staff numbered thousands; those who held the post before and after all amassed great wealth.
translations.idiomatic: A key town near the capital, its staff numbered thousands; every predecessor had grown rich.

sentences.zh: 洽清身率職，饋遺一無所受，妻子不免饑寒。

translations.literal: Qia kept himself pure and led his office honestly, accepting no gifts; his wife and children did not escape hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Qia kept himself pure and honest in office, accepting no gifts; his wife and children still knew hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 累遷臨海太守，為政清平，不尚威猛，人俗便之。

translations.literal: Promoted repeatedly to Administrator of Linhai; his governance was clear and even, not relying on severity; the people found him easy to live under.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to administrator of Linhai, he governed clearly and evenly without severity; the people found him easy to live under.

sentences.zh: 還拜司徒左長史。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed Chief Secretary of the Left to the Minister of Masses.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was made chief secretary to the left of the Minister of Masses.

sentences.zh: 敕撰當塗堰碑，辭甚贍麗。

translations.literal: By edict he composed the stele for the Dangtu weir; the text was very rich and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: By edict he wrote the stele for the Dangtu weir; the text was rich and elegant.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 文集二十卷行於世。

translations.literal: His collected writings in twenty scrolls circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings in twenty scrolls circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 惠基弟惠休。

translations.literal: Huiji's younger brother Huixiu.
translations.idiomatic: Huiji's younger brother Huixiu.

sentences.zh: 齊永明四年，為廣州刺史，罷任，獻奉傾資。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongming of Qi he was Governor of Guang Province; on leaving office he presented tribute with his entire fortune.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi Yongming's fourth year he governed Guang Province; on leaving he presented tribute with his entire fortune.

sentences.zh: 上敕中書舍人茹法亮曰：「可問蕭惠休，故當不復私邪？

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Secretariat Gentleman Ru Faliang, "You may ask Xiao Huixiu — surely he will not be corrupt again?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered secretariat gentleman Ru Faliang, "Ask Xiao Huixiu — surely he will not be corrupt again?

sentences.zh: 吾欲分受之也。

translations.literal: I wish to share in receiving it.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to share in receiving it.

sentences.zh: 」後封建安縣子。

translations.literal: Later he was enfeoffed Viscount of Jian'an county.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was enfeoffed viscount of Jian'an county.

sentences.zh: 永元元年，徙吳興太守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan he was transferred to Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan's first year he was moved to administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 徵為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Vice Minister of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as vice minister of the right.

sentences.zh: 吳興郡項羽神舊酷烈，人云惠休事神謹，故得美遷。

translations.literal: In Wuxing the spirit of Xiang Yu had long been fierce; people said Huixiu served the spirit carefully and therefore received a fine promotion.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuxing the spirit of Xiang Yu had long been fierce; people said Huixiu served the spirit carefully and therefore won a fine promotion.

sentences.zh: 于時朝士多見殺，二年，惠休還至平望，帝令服藥而卒，贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At that time many court officials were killed; in the second year Huixiu, returning, reached Pingwang; the Emperor had him take poison and die; posthumously he was given Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Many court officials were being killed; in the second year Huixiu, returning, reached Pingwang; the emperor had him take poison and die, and posthumously gave him Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 惠休弟惠朗，同桂陽賊，齊高帝赦之。

translations.literal: Huixiu's younger brother Huilang joined Prince Guiyang's rebellion; Emperor Gao of Qi pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Huixiu's younger brother Huilang joined Prince Guiyang's rebellion; Emperor Gao of Qi pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 後為西陽王征虜長史，行南兗州事，坐法免官。

translations.literal: Later he was Chief Administrator to Prince Xiyang, General Who Subdues the Barbarians, acting in Southern Yan Province affairs; for an offense of law he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was chief administrator to Prince Xiyang as General Who Subdues the Barbarians, acting in Southern Yan affairs; for a legal offense he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 惠朗弟惠蒨，仕齊左戶尚書。

translations.literal: Huilang's younger brother Huiqian served Qi as Minister of the Left Household.
translations.idiomatic: Huilang's younger brother Huiqian served Qi as minister of the left household.

sentences.zh: 子介。

translations.literal: His son Jie.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jie.

sentences.zh: 介字茂鏡，少穎悟，有器識。

translations.literal: Jie, styled Maojing, was quick and perceptive from youth with capacity and discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Jie, courtesy name Maojing, was quick and perceptive from youth with capacity and discernment.

sentences.zh: 梁大同中，武陵王紀為揚州刺史，以介為府長史，在職以清白稱。

translations.literal: In Liang's Datong era Prince Wu Ling Ji governed Yang Province and made Jie chief administrator of his household; in office he was famed for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang's Datong era Prince Wu Ling Ji governed Yang Province and made Jie chief administrator of his household; in office he was famed for integrity.

sentences.zh: 武帝謂何敬容曰：「蕭介甚貧，可處以一郡。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu said to He Jingrong, "Xiao Jie is very poor — he may be given a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu told He Jingrong, "Xiao Jie is very poor — he may be given a commandery.

sentences.zh: 」復曰：「始興郡頻無良守，可以介為之。

translations.literal: He also said, "Shixing Commandery has often lacked good administrators — Jie may be sent there.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Shixing has often lacked good administrators — Jie may go there.

sentences.zh: 」由是出為始興太守。

translations.literal: For this he went out as Administrator of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: For this he went out as administrator of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 及至，甚著威德。

translations.literal: On reaching his post he showed great authority and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post he showed great authority and virtue.

sentences.zh: 徵為少府卿，尋加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Director of the Palace Storehouse and soon added Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as director of the palace storehouse and soon added regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 會侍中闕，選司舉王筠等四人，並不稱旨。

translations.literal: When the attendant's post fell vacant the selection office proposed Wang Yun and three others; none pleased the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When the attendant's post fell vacant the selection office proposed Wang Yun and three others; none pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我門中久無此職，宜用蕭介為之。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "My household has long lacked this office — Xiao Jie should fill it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "My household has long lacked this office — Xiao Jie should fill it.

sentences.zh: 」應對左右，多所匡正，帝甚重之。

translations.literal: In audience before and beside the throne he often corrected matters; the Emperor greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: In audience he often corrected matters; the emperor greatly valued him.

sentences.zh: 遷都官尚書，每軍國大事，必先訪介。

translations.literal: Promoted to Minister of Justice, on every great affair of state and army the Emperor first consulted Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to minister of justice, on every great affair of state and army the emperor first consulted Jie.

sentences.zh: 帝謂朱異曰：「端右材也。

translations.literal: The Emperor told Zhu Yi, "He is material for the right hand of power.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Zhu Yi, "He is material for the right hand of power.

sentences.zh: 」中大同二年，辭疾致仕，帝優詔不許，終不肯起，乃遣謁者僕射魏祥就拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongdatong he pleaded illness to retire; the Emperor's gracious edict would not allow it; he still refused to rise; then an envoy, Vice Director of the Imperial Household Wei Xiang, was sent to invest him as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongdatong's second year he pleaded illness to retire; the emperor's gracious edict would not allow it; he still refused to rise; then envoy Vice Director of the Imperial Household Wei Xiang was sent to invest him as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 太清中，侯景于渦陽敗走，入壽陽。

translations.literal: In the Taqing era Hou Jing, defeated at Woyang, fled into Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Taqing Hou Jing, defeated at Woyang, fled into Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 帝敕助防韋黯納之，介聞而上表致諫，極言不可。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Assistant Defender Wei An to admit him; Jie heard and submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying most strongly that it must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered assistant defender Wei An to admit him; Jie heard and submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying most strongly that it must not be done.

sentences.zh: 帝省表歎息，卒不能用。

translations.literal: The Emperor read the memorial, sighed, and in the end could not use it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial, sighed, and in the end could not heed it.

sentences.zh: 介性高簡，少交遊，唯與族兄琛、從兄視素及洽從弟淑等文酒賞會，時人以比謝氏烏衣之遊。

translations.literal: Jie by nature was lofty and spare, with few social ties; only with his clan elder Chen, his cousin Shisu, and Qia's cousin Shu did he meet for wine, letters, and pleasure — men of the time compared it to the Wuyi outings of the Xie clan.
translations.idiomatic: Jie by nature was lofty and spare, with few social ties; only with his clan elder Chen, cousin Shisu, and Qia's cousin Shu did he meet for wine, letters, and pleasure — men of the time compared it to the Xie clan's Wuyi outings.

sentences.zh: 初，武帝招延後進二十餘人，置酒賦詩。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Wu gathered more than twenty rising scholars, set out wine, and assigned poems.
translations.idiomatic: At first Emperor Wu gathered more than twenty rising scholars, set out wine, and assigned poems.

sentences.zh: 臧盾以詩不成，罰酒一斗。

translations.literal: Zang Dun failed to compose a poem and was fined one dipper of wine.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Dun failed to compose a poem and was fined one dipper of wine.

sentences.zh: 盾飲盡，顏色不變，言笑自若。

translations.literal: Dun drank it all; his color did not change and he spoke and laughed as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Dun drank it all; his color did not change and he spoke and laughed as usual.

sentences.zh: 介染翰便成，文無加點。

translations.literal: Jie took up the brush and finished at once; the text needed no correction.
translations.idiomatic: Jie took up the brush and finished at once, the text needing no correction.

sentences.zh: 帝兩美之曰：「臧盾之飲，蕭介之文，即席之美也。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised both, saying, "Zang Dun's drinking and Xiao Jie's writing — the beauty of the moment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised both: "Zang Dun's drinking and Xiao Jie's writing — the beauty of the moment.

sentences.zh: 」年七十三，卒於家。

translations.literal: At seventy-three he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy-three he died at home.

sentences.zh: 第三子允字叔佐，少知名。

translations.literal: His third son Yun, styled Shuzuo, was known from youth.
translations.idiomatic: His third son Yun, courtesy name Shuzuo, was known from youth.

sentences.zh: 風神凝遠，通達有識鑒，容止醞藉。

translations.literal: His spirit was concentrated and far-reaching; he was penetrating with discernment; his bearing was refined and restrained.
translations.idiomatic: His spirit was concentrated and far-reaching; he was penetrating and discerning; his bearing was refined and restrained.

sentences.zh: 仕梁位太子洗馬。

translations.literal: Serving Liang he held the post of Groom of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he served as groom of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 侯景攻陷台城，百僚奔散，允獨整衣冠坐于宮坊，景軍敬焉，弗之逼也。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing took Taicheng the hundred officials fled; Yun alone straightened cap and robe and sat in the palace ward; Jing's troops respected him and did not press him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing took Taicheng the hundred officials fled; Yun alone straightened cap and robe and sat in the palace ward; Jing's troops respected him and did not press him.

sentences.zh: 尋出居京口。

translations.literal: Soon after he went out to live at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he went out to live at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 時寇賊縱橫，百姓波駭，允獨不行。

translations.literal: When bandits ran wild and the people were thrown into panic, Yun alone did not flee.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits ran wild and the people panicked, Yun alone did not flee.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，允曰：「性命自有常分，豈可逃而免乎。

translations.literal: When men asked why, Yun said, "Life and fate have their fixed portion — how can one flee to escape?
translations.idiomatic: When men asked why, Yun said, "Life and fate have their fixed portion — how can one flee to escape?

sentences.zh: 方今百姓，爭欲奮臂而論大功，何事于一書生哉。

translations.literal: Now the common people all wish to raise their arms and talk of great merit — what matter is one bookish man?
translations.idiomatic: Now the common people all wish to raise their arms and talk of great merit — what matter is one bookish man?

sentences.zh: 莊周所謂畏影避跡，吾弗為也。

translations.literal: What Zhuang Zhou called fearing one's shadow and avoiding one's footprints — I will not do that.
translations.idiomatic: What Zhuang Zhou called fearing one's shadow and avoiding one's footprints — I will not do that.

sentences.zh: 」乃閉門靜處，並日而食，卒免於患。

translations.literal: He then shut his door and lived quietly, eating once every other day, and in the end escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: He shut his door and lived quietly, eating once every other day, and in the end escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 允性敦重，未嘗以榮利幹懷。

translations.literal: Yun by nature was solid and grave and never let profit and honor touch his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yun by nature was solid and grave and never let profit or honor touch his heart.

sentences.zh: 及晉安出鎮湘州，又苦攜允。

translations.literal: When Prince Jin'an went out to govern Xiang Province he again pressed Yun to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jin'an went out to govern Xiang Province he again pressed Yun to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 允少與蔡景曆善，子征修父党之敬，聞允將行，乃詣允曰：「公年德並高，國之元老，從容坐鎮，旦夕自為列曹，何為方辛苦蕃外。

translations.literal: Yun from youth had been friendly with Cai Jingli; Zheng's son Zhengxiu showed the respect due a father's friend; hearing Yun was to go, he came to Yun and said, "Sir, your years and virtue are both high, the state's elder — to sit at ease in command, morning and evening you would be among the chief ministers; why go out in hardship to the frontier?
translations.idiomatic: Yun had been friendly with Cai Jingli from youth; Zheng's son Zhengxiu showed a father's friend's respect; hearing Yun was to go, he came and said, "Sir, your years and virtue are both high — the state's elder; to sit at ease in command you would be among the chief ministers morning and evening; why go out in hardship to the frontier?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「已許晉安，豈可忘信。

translations.literal: He answered, "I have already promised Jin'an — how can I forget faith?
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I have already promised Jin'an — how can I break faith?

sentences.zh: 」其恬榮勢如此。

translations.literal: Such was his indifference to glory and power.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his indifference to glory and power.

sentences.zh: 至德中，鄱陽王出鎮會稽，允又為長史，帶會稽郡丞。

translations.literal: In the Zhide era Prince Poyang went out to govern Kuaiji; Yun again served as chief administrator and concurrently as assistant administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide Prince Poyang went out to govern Kuaiji; Yun again served as chief administrator and concurrently as assistant administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 行經延陵季子廟，設蘋藻之薦，托異代之交，為詩以敘意，辭理清典。

translations.literal: Passing the temple of Master Ji of Yanling he set out offerings of duckweed and algae and, invoking friendship across ages, composed a poem to express his intent — the wording clear and classical.
translations.idiomatic: Passing the temple of Master Ji of Yanling he set out offerings of duckweed and algae and, invoking friendship across ages, composed a poem to express his intent — the wording clear and classical.

sentences.zh: 後主嘗問蔡征，允之為人，征曰：「其清虛玄遠，殆不可測；

translations.literal: The Later Lord once asked Cai Zheng about Yun's character; Zheng said, "His clarity and remoteness are perhaps beyond measure;
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord once asked Cai Zheng about Yun's character; Zheng said, "His clarity and remoteness are perhaps beyond measure;

sentences.zh: 至於文章，可得而言。

translations.literal: as for his writing, one may speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: as for his writing, one may speak of it.

sentences.zh: 」因誦允詩以對。

translations.literal: He then recited Yun's poem in reply.
translations.idiomatic: He then recited Yun's poem in reply.

sentences.zh: 後主嗟賞久之。

translations.literal: The Later Lord sighed in admiration for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord sighed in admiration for a long time.

sentences.zh: 尋拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 及隋師濟江，允遷于關右。

translations.literal: When the Sui army crossed the river Yun moved to the lands west of the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui army crossed the river Yun moved to the lands west of the Pass.

sentences.zh: 時南士至長安者，例皆授官，允與尚書僕射謝伷辭以老疾。

translations.literal: At that time southerners who reached Chang'an were by rule all given office; Yun and Vice Minister of the Left Xie You pleaded old age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: At that time southerners who reached Chang'an were by rule all given office; Yun and Vice Minister of the Left Xie You pleaded old age and illness.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝義之，並厚賜帛。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui approved their righteousness and richly bestowed silk on both.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui approved their righteousness and richly bestowed silk on both.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年八十四。

translations.literal: Soon after he died, aged eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he died, aged eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 弟引字叔休，方正有器度，性聰敏，博學善屬文。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yin, styled Shuxiu, was upright with capacity; clever by nature, he learned widely and wrote well.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yin, courtesy name Shuxiu, was upright with capacity; clever by nature, he learned widely and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 仕梁位西昌侯儀同府主簿。

translations.literal: Serving Liang he held the post of Master of Records in the Marquis of Xichang's household with the rank of Equal to the Three Lords.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he served as master of records in the Marquis of Xichang's household with rank equal to the Three Lords.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，梁元帝為荊州刺史，朝士多歸之。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Emperor Yuan of Liang was Governor of Jing Province and court officials mostly went to him.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion Emperor Yuan of Liang was governor of Jing Province and court officials mostly went to him.

sentences.zh: 引曰：「諸王力爭，禍患方始，今日逃難，未是擇君之秋。

translations.literal: Yin said, "The princes are contending and disaster is just beginning; to flee now is not the season for choosing a lord.
translations.idiomatic: Yin said, "The princes are contending and disaster is just beginning; to flee now is not the season for choosing a lord.

sentences.zh: 吾家再世為始興郡，遺愛在人，政可南行以存家門耳。

translations.literal: Our house has for two generations held Shixing Commandery; kindness left with the people remains; we may rightly go south to preserve the family gate.
translations.idiomatic: Our house has governed Shixing for two generations; kindness left with the people remains; we may rightly go south to preserve the family gate.

sentences.zh: 」乃與弟肜及宗親等百餘人南奔嶺表。

translations.literal: He then fled south beyond the ranges with his younger brother Rong and more than a hundred kin.
translations.idiomatic: He then fled south beyond the ranges with his younger brother Rong and more than a hundred kin.

sentences.zh: 時始興人歐陽頠為衡州刺史，乃往依焉。

translations.literal: At that time Ouyang Yu of Shixing was Governor of Heng Province; they went to rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ouyang Yu of Shixing was governor of Heng Province; they went to rely on him.

sentences.zh: 頠遷廣州病死，子紇領其眾，引疑紇異圖，因事規正，由是情禮漸疏。

translations.literal: Yu was transferred to Guang Province and died on the road; his son He led the host; Yin suspected He's divergent intent and, by correcting affairs, drew gradually apart in feeling and courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was transferred to Guang Province and died on the road; his son He led the host; Yin suspected He's divergent intent and, by correcting affairs, drew gradually apart in feeling and courtesy.

sentences.zh: 及紇反，時都下士人岑之敬、公孫挺等並惶駭，唯引怡然，謂之敬等曰：「管幼安、袁曜卿亦但安坐耳。

translations.literal: When He rebelled, scholars at the capital such as Cen Zhijing and Gongsun Ting were all terrified; only Yin was at ease and told Zhijing and the rest, "Guan You'an and Yuan Yaoging also simply sat at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When He rebelled, capital scholars such as Cen Zhijing and Gongsun Ting were terrified; only Yin was at ease and told them, "Guan You'an and Yuan Yaoging also simply sat at ease.

sentences.zh: 君子正身以明道，直己以行義，亦何憂乎。

translations.literal: The gentleman rectifies himself to make the Way clear and straightens himself to act with righteousness — why worry?
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman rectifies himself to make the Way clear and straightens himself to act with righteousness — why worry?

sentences.zh: 」及章昭達平番禺，引始北還，拜尚書金部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Zhang Zhaoda pacified Panyu Yin at last returned north and was appointed Gentleman of the Gold Department of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhaoda pacified Panyu Yin at last returned north and was appointed gentleman of the gold department of the ministry of revenue.

sentences.zh: 引善隸書，為當時所重，宣帝嘗披奏事，指引署名曰：「此字筆趣翩翩，似鳥之欲飛。

translations.literal: Yin was skilled at clerical script and was valued in his time; Emperor Xuan, reading memorials, pointed to Yin's signature and said, "This script's brush-intent is light and soaring, like a bird about to fly.
translations.idiomatic: Yin wrote clerical script well and was valued in his time; Emperor Xuan, reading memorials, pointed to Yin's signature and said, "This script's brush-intent is light and soaring, like a bird about to fly.

sentences.zh: 」引謝曰：「此乃陛下假其毛羽耳。

translations.literal: Yin thanked him, "This is simply Your Majesty lending it feathers.
translations.idiomatic: Yin thanked him, "This is simply Your Majesty lending it feathers.

sentences.zh: 」帝又謂引曰：「我每有所忿，見卿輒意解，何也？

translations.literal: The Emperor also said to Yin, "Whenever I am angry, seeing you my mind clears — why?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also said to Yin, "Whenever I am angry, seeing you my mind clears — why?

sentences.zh: 」引曰：「此自陛下不遷怒，臣何預此恩。」

translations.literal: Yin said, "That is simply Your Majesty not shifting anger — how could your servant share in this grace?"
translations.idiomatic: Yin said, "That is simply Your Majesty not shifting anger — how could your servant share in this grace?"

sentences.zh: 引性抗直，不事權貴，宣帝每欲遷用，輒為用事者所裁。

translations.literal: Yin by nature was upright and did not serve the powerful; whenever the Emperor wished to promote him, those in power cut it short.
translations.idiomatic: Yin by nature was upright and did not serve the powerful; whenever the emperor wished to promote him, those in power cut it short.

sentences.zh: 及呂梁覆師，戎儲空匱，轉引為庫部侍郎，掌知營造。

translations.literal: When the Lüliang army was destroyed and military stores were empty, Yin was transferred to Gentleman of the Storehouse Department and put in charge of construction.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lüliang army was destroyed and military stores were empty, Yin was transferred to gentleman of the storehouse department and put in charge of construction.

sentences.zh: 引在職一年，而器械充足。

translations.literal: Yin held the post one year and equipment was ample.
translations.idiomatic: Yin held the post one year and equipment was ample.

sentences.zh: 曆中書，黃門，吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He served successively at the Secretariat, Yellow Gate, and as Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively at the secretariat, Yellow Gate, and as gentleman of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 廣州刺史馬靖甚得嶺表人心，而甲兵精練，每年深入俚洞，數有戰功，朝野頗生異議。

translations.literal: Guang Province Inspector Ma Jing won the hearts of the people beyond the ranges; his armor and troops were well trained; each year he penetrated deep into the Li caves and often won battles; court and realm both grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Guang inspector Ma Jing won hearts beyond the ranges; his armor and troops were well trained; each year he penetrated deep into the Li caves and often won battles; court and realm both grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 宣帝以引悉嶺外物情，且遣引觀靖，審其舉措，諷令送質。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan, because Yin knew conditions beyond the ranges well and also sent Yin to observe Jing and judge his conduct, hinted that he should send hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan, because Yin knew conditions beyond the ranges well, also sent Yin to observe Jing and judge his conduct, hinting that he should send hostages.

sentences.zh: 及至，靖即悟旨，遣兒弟為質。

translations.literal: When he arrived Jing at once understood the intent and sent his younger brothers as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived Jing at once understood the intent and sent his younger brothers as hostages.

sentences.zh: 琛少明悟，有才辯。

translations.literal: Chen from youth was bright and perceptive, with talent in debate.
translations.idiomatic: Chen from youth was bright and perceptive, with talent in debate.

sentences.zh: 數歲時，從伯惠開見而奇之，撫其背曰：「必興吾宗。

translations.literal: When only a few years old his uncle Huikai saw him and marveled; stroking his back he said, "You will surely raise our clan.
translations.idiomatic: When only a few years old his uncle Huikai saw him and marveled; stroking his back he said, "You will surely raise our clan.

sentences.zh: 」起家齊太學博士。

translations.literal: He began his career as Doctor of the Grand Learning of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as doctor of the grand learning of Qi.

sentences.zh: 時王儉當朝，琛年少，未為儉所識。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Jian held the court; Chen was young and had not yet been noticed by Jian.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Jian held the court; Chen was young and had not yet been noticed by Jian.

sentences.zh: 負其才氣，候儉宴于樂遊，乃著虎皮靴，策桃枝杖，直造儉坐。

translations.literal: Trusting his talent and spirit, he waited for Jian's banquet at Leyou, then wore tiger-skin boots, grasped a peach-branch staff, and went straight to Jian's seat.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting his talent and spirit, he waited for Jian's banquet at Leyou, then wore tiger-skin boots, grasped a peach-branch staff, and went straight to Jian's seat.

sentences.zh: 儉與語大悅。

translations.literal: Jian spoke with him and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Jian spoke with him and was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 儉時為丹陽尹，辟為主簿。

translations.literal: Jian was then Magistrate of Danyang and summoned him as Master of Records.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was then magistrate of Danyang and summoned him as master of records.

sentences.zh: 永明九年，魏始通好，琛再銜命北使，還為通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongming Wei first opened friendly relations; Chen twice carried orders as envoy north and on return was Regular Attendant and General of Unimpeded Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming's ninth year Wei first opened friendly relations; Chen twice carried orders as envoy north and on return was regular attendant and general of unimpeded cavalry.

sentences.zh: 時魏遣李彪來使，齊武帝燕之。

translations.literal: At that time Wei sent Li Biao as envoy; Emperor Wu of Qi feasted him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wei sent Li Biao as envoy; Emperor Wu of Qi feasted him.

sentences.zh: 琛於御筵舉酒勸彪，彪不受，曰：「公庭無私禮，不容受勸。

translations.literal: At the imperial banquet Chen raised wine to urge Biao; Biao did not accept and said, "In the public hall there is no private courtesy — I cannot accept urging.
translations.idiomatic: At the imperial banquet Chen raised wine to urge Biao; Biao did not accept and said, "In the public hall there is no private courtesy — I cannot accept urging.

sentences.zh: 」琛答曰：「詩所謂'雨我公田，遂及我私'。

translations.literal: Chen answered, "The Odes say, 'Rain on our public field, and reaches our private field.'
translations.idiomatic: Chen answered, "The Odes say, 'Rain on our public field, and reaches our private field.'

sentences.zh: 」坐者皆悅服，彪乃受琛酒。

translations.literal: Those seated were all pleased and submitted; Biao then accepted Chen's wine.
translations.idiomatic: Those seated were all pleased and submitted; Biao then accepted Chen's wine.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Promoted repeatedly to Left Assistant Minister of the Secretariat.
