translations.idiomatic: Promoted repeatedly to left assistant minister of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時齊明帝用法嚴峻，尚書郎坐杖罰者皆即科行，琛乃密啟曰：「郎有杖起自後漢，爾時郎官位卑，親主文案，與令史不異。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Ming of Qi used the law with harsh severity; Secretariat Gentlemen who sat for beating were immediately punished; Chen then secretly memorialized, "Beating of Gentlemen began in Later Han, when the Gentleman's post was low and he personally handled documents, no different from a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Ming of Qi used the law with harsh severity; secretariat gentlemen who sat for beating were immediately punished; Chen then secretly memorialized, "Beating of gentlemen began in Later Han, when the gentleman's post was low and he personally handled documents, no different from a clerk.

sentences.zh: 故郎三十五人，令史二十人，是以古人多恥為此職。

translations.literal: Thus there were thirty-five Gentlemen and twenty clerks — therefore men of old often felt shame at this office.
translations.idiomatic: Thus there were thirty-five gentlemen and twenty clerks — therefore men of old often felt shame at this office.

sentences.zh: 自魏、晉以來，郎官稍重。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin onward the Gentleman's post grew somewhat weightier.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin onward the gentleman's post grew somewhat weightier.

sentences.zh: 今方參用高華，吏部又近於通貴，不應官高昔品，而罰遵曩科。

translations.literal: Now high and splendid men are jointly employed and the Ministry of Personnel is again close to passing nobility — one should not keep high office with old rank and punish by former statute.
translations.idiomatic: Now high and splendid men are jointly employed and the ministry of personnel is again close to passing nobility — one should not keep high office with old rank and punish by former statute.

sentences.zh: 所以從來彈舉，雖在空文，而許以推遷。

translations.literal: Therefore impeachments from the past, though empty in text, were allowed deferral of transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore impeachments from the past, though empty in text, were allowed deferral of transfer.

sentences.zh: 或逢赦恩，或入春令，便得息停。

translations.literal: Sometimes on meeting amnesty, sometimes entering spring ordinance, punishment would cease.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes on meeting amnesty, sometimes entering spring ordinance, punishment would cease.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉、大明中，經有被罰者，別由犯忤主心，非關常准。

translations.literal: In Yuanjia and Daming of Song there were those beaten, but that was for offending the ruler's heart, not the usual standard.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia and Daming of Song there were those beaten, but that was for offending the ruler's heart, not the usual standard.

sentences.zh: 自泰始、建元以來，未經施行，事廢已久，人情未習。

translations.literal: From Taishi and Jianyuan onward it had not been applied; the practice had long ceased and men's hearts were unaccustomed.
translations.idiomatic: From Taishi and Jianyuan onward it had not been applied; the practice had long ceased and men's hearts were unaccustomed.

sentences.zh: 自奉敕之後，已行倉部郎江重欣杖督五十，皆無不人懷慚懼。

translations.literal: Since receiving the edict, Treasury Department Gentleman Jiang Chongxin had already been beaten fifty strokes — all without exception felt shame and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Since receiving the edict, treasury department gentleman Jiang Chongxin had already been beaten fifty strokes — all without exception felt shame and fear.

sentences.zh: 兼有子弟成長，彌復難為儀適。

translations.literal: Moreover sons and younger brothers have grown up — it is all the harder for proper bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover sons and younger brothers have grown up — it is all the harder for proper bearing.

sentences.zh: 其應行罰，可特賜輸贖，使與令史有異，以彰優緩之澤。

translations.literal: Those who should be punished may specially be allowed ransom by payment, so they differ from clerks and the grace of leniency is shown.
translations.idiomatic: Those who should be punished may specially be allowed ransom by payment, so they differ from clerks and the grace of leniency is shown.

sentences.zh: 」帝納之。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this.

sentences.zh: 自是應受罰者，依舊不行。

translations.literal: From this those who should be beaten were as before not beaten.
translations.idiomatic: From this those who should be beaten were as before not beaten.

sentences.zh: 東昏初嗣立，時議無廟見文。

translations.literal: When Eastern Depravity first succeeded, at that time discussion lacked the text for temple audience on accession.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Depravity first succeeded, discussion lacked the text for temple audience on accession.

sentences.zh: 琛議據周頌烈文、閔予，皆為即位朝廟之典。

translations.literal: Chen argued from the Zhou Odes Lie Wen and Min Yu, both being canons for accession audience at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Chen argued from the Zhou Odes Lie Wen and Min Yu, both being canons for accession audience at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 於是從之。

translations.literal: They therefore followed this.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore followed this.

sentences.zh: 梁武在西邸，與琛有舊。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang, while in the Western Residence, had old ties with Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang, while in the Western Residence, had old ties with Chen.

sentences.zh: 梁台建，以為御史中丞。

translations.literal: When the Liang regime was established he was made Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang regime was established he was made imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 天監九年，累遷平西長史、江夏太守。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianjian he was promoted repeatedly to Chief Administrator of Pacifying the West and Administrator of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian's ninth year he was promoted repeatedly to chief administrator of Pacifying the West and administrator of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 始琛為宣城太守，有北僧南度，唯齎一瓠蘆，中有漢書序傳。

translations.literal: At first when Chen was Administrator of Xuancheng a northern monk came south carrying only a gourd, inside which was the Han Shu narrative biography.
translations.idiomatic: At first when Chen was administrator of Xuancheng a northern monk came south carrying only a gourd, inside which was the Han Shu narrative biography.

sentences.zh: 僧云：「三輔舊老相傳，以為班固真本。

translations.literal: The monk said, "Old men of the three metropolitan regions transmit that this is Ban Gu's authentic original.
translations.idiomatic: The monk said, "Old men of the three metropolitan regions transmit that this is Ban Gu's authentic original.

sentences.zh: 」琛固求得之，其書多有異今者，而紙墨亦古，文字多如龍舉之例，非隸非篆。

translations.literal: Chen firmly sought to obtain it; the book differed in many places from the present version, and the paper and ink were also old; the characters were often like the pattern of a dragon rising — neither clerical nor seal.
translations.idiomatic: Chen firmly sought to obtain it; the book differed in many places from the present version, and the paper and ink were also old; the characters were often like the pattern of a dragon rising — neither clerical nor seal.

sentences.zh: 琛甚秘之。

translations.literal: Chen kept it very secret.
translations.idiomatic: Chen kept it very secret.

sentences.zh: 及是以書餉鄱陽王范，獻於東宮。

translations.literal: For this he presented the book to Prince Poyang Fan and offered it to the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: For this he presented the book to Prince Poyang Fan and offered it to the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 後為吳興太守，郡有項羽廟，土人名為「憤王」，甚有靈驗，遂於郡聽事安床幕為神座，公私請禱。

translations.literal: Later as Administrator of Wuxing, in the commandery was a temple to Xiang Yu; the locals called him "Indignant King" — it was very efficacious; he therefore set bed and curtain in the commandery hall as a spirit seat, and public and private alike prayed there.
translations.idiomatic: Later as administrator of Wuxing, in the commandery was a temple to Xiang Yu; the locals called him Indignant King — it was very efficacious; he set bed and curtain in the commandery hall as a spirit seat, and public and private alike prayed there.

sentences.zh: 前後二千石皆於聽拜祠，以軛下牛充祭而避居他室。

translations.literal: Former and later administrators of two thousand households all worshipped in the hall, using oxen from under the yoke for sacrifice and moving to other quarters to avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: Former and later administrators all worshipped in the hall, using oxen from under the yoke for sacrifice and moving to other quarters to avoid it.

sentences.zh: 琛至，著履登聽事，聞室中有叱聲。

translations.literal: When Chen arrived he wore shoes and ascended the hall; he heard a shout from within the room.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen arrived he wore shoes and ascended the hall; he heard a shout from within the room.

sentences.zh: 琛厲色曰：「生不能與漢祖爭中原，死據此聽事，何也？

translations.literal: Chen sternly said, "Alive you could not contend with the Han Founder for the Central Plains — dead you occupy this hall, why?
translations.idiomatic: Chen sternly said, "Alive you could not contend with the Han Founder for the Central Plains — dead you occupy this hall, why?

sentences.zh: 」因遷之於廟。

translations.literal: He then moved the spirit to the temple.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved the spirit to the temple.

sentences.zh: 又禁殺牛解祀，以脯代肉。

translations.literal: He also forbade killing oxen for sacrifice and used dried meat instead of fresh.
translations.idiomatic: He also forbade killing oxen for sacrifice and used dried meat instead of fresh.

sentences.zh: 琛頻蒞大郡，不事產業，有闕則取，不以為嫌。

translations.literal: Chen repeatedly governed great commanderies and did not pursue estates; when there was shortage he took — he did not consider it shameful.
translations.idiomatic: Chen repeatedly governed great commanderies and did not pursue estates; when there was shortage he took — he did not consider it shameful.

sentences.zh: 曆左戶、度支二尚書，侍中。

translations.literal: He served successively as Minister of the Left Household, Minister of Revenue, and Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as minister of the left household, minister of revenue, and attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 帝每朝燕，接琛以舊恩。

translations.literal: Whenever the Emperor held morning feast Chen was received for old favor.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor held morning feast Chen was received for old favor.

sentences.zh: 嘗犯武帝偏諱，帝斂容。

translations.literal: Once he violated the Emperor's partial taboo; the Emperor composed his face.
translations.idiomatic: Once he violated the emperor's partial taboo; the emperor composed his face.

sentences.zh: 琛從容曰：「二名不偏諱。

translations.literal: Chen calmly said, "The two names are not both tabooed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen calmly said, "The two names are not both tabooed.

sentences.zh: 陛下不應諱順。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should not taboo Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should not taboo Shun.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「各有家風。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Each house has its own custom.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Each house has its own custom.

sentences.zh: 」琛曰：「其如禮何。

translations.literal: Chen said, "But what of ritual?
translations.idiomatic: Chen said, "But what of ritual?

sentences.zh: 」又經預御筵醉伏，上以棗投琛，琛仍取栗擲上，正中面。

translations.literal: Again at an imperial banquet he drank himself drunk and collapsed; the Emperor threw jujubes at Chen; Chen took chestnuts and threw back at the Emperor, hitting him square in the face.
translations.idiomatic: Again at an imperial banquet he drank himself drunk and collapsed; the emperor threw jujubes at Chen; Chen took chestnuts and threw back, hitting him square in the face.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞在坐，帝動色曰：「此中有人，不得如此，豈有說邪？

translations.literal: The Imperial Censor was seated; the Emperor changed color and said, "There are people here — you cannot do this; is there no explanation?
translations.idiomatic: The imperial censor was seated; the emperor changed color and said, "There are people here — you cannot do this; is there no explanation?

sentences.zh: 」琛即答曰：「陛下投臣以赤心，臣敢不報以戰慄。

translations.literal: Chen at once answered, "Your Majesty threw your servant a loyal heart; your servant dares not reply except with trembling.
translations.idiomatic: Chen at once answered, "Your Majesty threw your servant a loyal heart; your servant dares not reply except with trembling.

sentences.zh: 」上笑悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and was pleased.

sentences.zh: 上每呼琛為宗老，琛亦奉陳昔恩，以「早簉中陽，夙忝同閈，雖迷興運，猶荷洪慈」。

translations.literal: The Emperor often called Chen "Clan Elder"; Chen also offered past favor, saying, "Early we shared Zhongyang, long I have owed the same gate — though I missed the rise of fortune, I still bear great kindness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often called Chen "Clan Elder"; Chen also offered past favor, saying, "Early we shared Zhongyang, long I have owed the same gate — though I missed the rise of fortune, I still bear great kindness.

sentences.zh: 上答曰：「雖云早契闊，乃自非同志。

translations.literal: The Emperor answered, "Though we parted early, we were never of one mind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered, "Though we parted early, we were never of one mind.

sentences.zh: 勿談興運初，且道狂奴異。」

translations.literal: Do not speak of the fortune's beginning — speak rather of the mad slave's strangeness."
translations.idiomatic: Do not speak of the fortune's beginning — speak rather of the mad slave's strangeness."

sentences.zh: 琛常言：「少壯三好：音律、書、酒。

translations.literal: Chen often said, "In youth I had three loves: music, books, and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Chen often said, "In youth I had three loves: music, books, and wine.

sentences.zh: 年長以來，二事都廢；

translations.literal: As the years grew, two were abandoned;
translations.idiomatic: As the years grew, two were abandoned;

sentences.zh: 唯書籍不衰。

translations.literal: only books did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: only books did not decline.

sentences.zh: 」而琛性通脫，常自解灶，事畢餘餕，必陶然致醉。

translations.literal: Yet Chen by nature was free and open; he often cooked for himself; when the task was done and leftovers remained he would always grow pleasantly drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chen by nature was free and open; he often cooked for himself; when the task was done and leftovers remained he would always grow pleasantly drunk.

sentences.zh: 位特進、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His rank was Special Advancement and Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was Special Advancement and Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 卒，遺令諸子：「與妻同墳異藏，祭以蔬菜。

translations.literal: When he died he left orders to his sons, "Share a tomb with your mother but separate burial; sacrifice with vegetables only.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he left orders to his sons, "Share a tomb with your mother but separate burial; sacrifice with vegetables only.

sentences.zh: 葬止車十乘，事存率素。

translations.literal: The funeral should use no more than ten carriages; keep affairs plainly simple.
translations.idiomatic: The funeral should use no more than ten carriages; keep affairs plainly simple.

sentences.zh: 」乘輿臨哭甚哀，諡曰平子。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage came to mourn very sorrowfully; posthumous title was Pingzi.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage came to mourn very sorrowfully; posthumous title was Pingzi.

sentences.zh: 琛所撰漢書文府、齊梁拾遺，並諸文集，數十萬言。

translations.literal: Chen's Han Shu Literary Repository, Qi-Liang gleanings, and various collected writings amounted to several hundred thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's Han Shu Literary Repository, Qi-Liang gleanings, and various collected writings amounted to several hundred thousand words.

sentences.zh: 子遊，位少府卿。

translations.literal: His son You held the post of Director of the Palace Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: His son You held the post of director of the palace storehouse.

sentences.zh: 遊子密字士幾，幼聰敏，博學有文詞。

translations.literal: You's son Mi, styled Shiji, was clever and perceptive from infancy, learned widely with literary skill.
translations.idiomatic: You's son Mi, courtesy name Shiji, was clever and perceptive from infancy, learned widely with literary skill.

sentences.zh: 位黃門郎，太子中庶子，散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His posts were Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His posts were gentleman at the Yellow Gate, junior mentor of the heir apparent, and regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 臧燾字德仁，東莞莒人，宋武敬皇后兄也。

translations.literal: Zang Dao, styled Deren, was a man of Ju in Dongguan, elder brother of Empress Jing of Song Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Dao, courtesy name Deren, came from Ju in Dongguan and was the elder brother of Empress Jing of Song Wu.

sentences.zh: 少好學，善三禮，貧約自立，操行為鄉里所稱。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning and was skilled in the Three Rites; poor and self-restrained, his conduct was praised in his village.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and was skilled in the Three Rites; poor and self-restrained, his conduct was praised in his village.

sentences.zh: 晉太元中，衛將軍謝安始立國學，徐、兗二州刺史謝玄舉燾為助教。

translations.literal: In the Taiyuan era of Jin, General of the Guard Xie An first established the National University; Xu and Yan Inspectors Xie Xuan recommended Dao as Assistant Instructor.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin's Taiyuan era, General of the Guard Xie An first established the National University; Xu and Yan inspectors Xie Xuan recommended Dao as assistant instructor.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝追崇庶祖母宣太后，議者或謂宜配食中宗。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Jin posthumously honored his common grandmother Empress Dowager Xuan; some debaters held she should share sacrifice with Emperor Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu of Jin posthumously honored his common grandmother Empress Dowager Xuan; some debaters held she should share sacrifice with Emperor Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 燾議曰：「陽秋之義，母以子貴，故仲子、成風咸稱夫人。

translations.literal: Dao argued, "The meaning of the Spring and Autumn is that the mother is honored through the son; therefore Zhongzi and Chengfeng are both called lady.
translations.idiomatic: Dao argued, "The meaning of the Spring and Autumn is that the mother is honored through the son; therefore Zhongzi and Chengfeng are both called lady.

sentences.zh: 經言考仲子宮，若配食惠廟，則宮無緣別築。

translations.literal: The classic speaks of examining Zhongzi's palace — if she shared sacrifice at Hui's temple, the palace would have no reason to be built separately.
translations.idiomatic: The classic speaks of examining Zhongzi's palace — if she shared sacrifice at Hui's temple, the palace would have no reason to be built separately.

sentences.zh: 前漢孝文孝昭太后並系子為號，祭於寢園，不配于高祖、孝武之廟。

translations.literal: Former Han's Empress Dowagers Xiaowen and Xiaozhao both took their titles from their sons and were sacrificed in the tomb park, not sharing the temples of Gaozu and Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Former Han's empress dowagers Xiaowen and Xiaozhao both took their titles from their sons and were sacrificed in the tomb park, not sharing the temples of Gaozu and Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 後漢和帝之母曰恭懷皇后，安帝祖母曰敬隱皇后，順帝之母曰恭湣皇后，雖不系子為號，亦祭於陵寢，不配章、安二帝。

translations.literal: Later Han's Empress Dowager Gonghuai of Emperor He, Empress Dowager Jingyin grandmother of Emperor An, and Empress Dowager Gongmin mother of Emperor Shun, though not taking titles from their sons, were also sacrificed at tomb parks, not sharing with Emperors Zhang and An.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han's empress dowager Gonghuai of Emperor He, empress dowager Jingyin grandmother of Emperor An, and empress dowager Gongmin mother of Emperor Shun, though not taking titles from their sons, were also sacrificed at tomb parks, not sharing with Emperors Zhang and An.

sentences.zh: 此則二漢雖有太后皇后之異，至於並不配食，義同陽秋。

translations.literal: Thus though Later and Former Han differ in whether empress dowager or empress, as to not sharing sacrifice the meaning matches the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Thus though Later and Former Han differ in whether empress dowager or empress, as to not sharing sacrifice the meaning matches the Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 唯光武追廢呂後，故以薄後配高廟。

translations.literal: Only Guangwu posthumously deposed Empress Lü, therefore Empress Bo shared Gaozu's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Only Guangwu posthumously deposed Empress Lü, therefore Empress Bo shared Gaozu's temple.

sentences.zh: 又衛後既廢，霍光追尊李夫人為皇后，配孝武廟。

translations.literal: Again when Empress Wei was deposed, Huo Guang posthumously honored Lady Li as empress and she shared Emperor Xiaowu's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Again when Empress Wei was deposed, Huo Guang posthumously honored Lady Li as empress and she shared Emperor Xiaowu's temple.

sentences.zh: 此非母以子貴之例，直以高、武二廟無配故耳。

translations.literal: This is not the case of the mother honored through the son — it is simply because Gaozu's and Xiaowu's temples had no consort.
translations.idiomatic: This is not the case of the mother honored through the son — it is simply because Gaozu's and Xiaowu's temples had no consort.

sentences.zh: 又漢世立寢於陵，自是晉制所異。

translations.literal: Again Han established tomb chambers at the mausoleum — this differs from Jin institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Again Han established tomb chambers at the mausoleum — this differs from Jin institutions.

sentences.zh: 謂宜遠准陽秋考宮之義，近慕二漢不配之典。

translations.literal: I hold that one should follow afar the Spring and Autumn meaning of examining the palace, and near emulate the two Han canon of not sharing sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that one should follow afar the Spring and Autumn meaning of examining the palace, and near emulate the two Han canon of not sharing sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 尊號既正，則罔極之情申，別建寢廟，則嚴禰之義顯。

translations.literal: Once the honored title is correct, boundless feeling is expressed; building a separate tomb-chamber temple then shows the meaning of honoring the near ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Once the honored title is correct, boundless feeling is expressed; building a separate tomb-chamber temple then shows the meaning of honoring the near ancestors.

sentences.zh: 系子為稱，兼明母貴之所由。

translations.literal: Taking the title from the son also clarifies whence the mother's honor comes.
translations.idiomatic: Taking the title from the son also clarifies whence the mother's honor comes.

sentences.zh: 一舉而允三義，固哲王之高致也。

translations.literal: One act satisfies three meanings — truly the lofty aim of a sage king.
translations.idiomatic: One act satisfies three meanings — truly the lofty aim of a sage king.

sentences.zh: 」議者從之。

translations.literal: The debaters followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The debaters followed this.

sentences.zh: 頃之去官，以父母老家貧，與弟熹俱棄人事，躬耕自業，約己養親者十餘年。

translations.literal: Soon after he left office; because his parents were old and the family poor, he and his younger brother Xi together abandoned worldly affairs, plowed for themselves, restrained themselves and nourished their parents for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he left office; because his parents were old and the family poor, he and his younger brother Xi together abandoned worldly affairs, plowed for themselves, restrained themselves and nourished their parents for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 父母喪亡，居喪六年，以毀瘠著稱。

translations.literal: When his parents died he observed mourning six years and was famed for grief-wasting.
translations.idiomatic: When his parents died he observed mourning six years and was famed for grief-wasting.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝義旗建，參右將軍何無忌軍事，隨府轉鎮南參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song raised the banner of righteousness he joined Right General He Wuji's staff and followed the headquarters to Staff Officer of Pacifying the South.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Song raised the banner of righteousness he joined Right General He Wuji's staff and followed the headquarters to staff officer of Pacifying the South.

sentences.zh: 武帝鎮京口，參帝中軍軍事，入補尚書度支郎，改掌祠部，襲封高陵亭侯。

translations.literal: When the Emperor garrisoned Jingkou he joined the Central Army staff, entered to fill the post of Gentleman of the Revenue Department, changed to control the Sacrifices Department, and inherited the enfeoffment Marquis of Gaoling district.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor garrisoned Jingkou he joined the central army staff, entered to fill the post of gentleman of the revenue department, changed to control the sacrifices department, and inherited the enfeoffment marquis of Gaoling district.

sentences.zh: 時太廟鴟尾災，燾謂著作郎徐廣曰：「昔孔子在齊聞魯廟災，曰必桓、僖也。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial temple's owl-tail finial burned; Dao told Compiler Xu Guang, "Formerly when Confucius was in Qi and heard of the Lu temple's disaster he said it must be Huan and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the imperial temple's owl-tail finial burned; Dao told compiler Xu Guang, "Formerly when Confucius was in Qi and heard of the Lu temple's disaster he said it must be Huan and Xi.

sentences.zh: 今征西、京兆四府君宜在毀落，而猶列廟饗，此其征乎。

translations.literal: Now the four lords of Pacifying the West and Jingzhao should be in the falling line and yet still stand in the temple sacrifices — is this not the sign?
translations.idiomatic: Now the four lords of Pacifying the West and Jingzhao should be in the falling line and yet still stand in the temple sacrifices — is this not the sign?

sentences.zh: 」乃上議曰：

translations.literal: He then submitted upstream a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted upstream a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞「國之大事，在祀與戎」。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard, "The state's great affairs are sacrifice and war."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard, "The state's great affairs are sacrifice and war."

sentences.zh: 將營宮室，宗廟為首。

translations.literal: When planning palace chambers, the ancestral temple comes first.
translations.idiomatic: When planning palace chambers, the ancestral temple comes first.

sentences.zh: 古先哲王莫不致肅恭之誠心，盡崇嚴乎祖考，然後能流淳化于四海，通幽感於神明，固宜詳廢興於古典，循情禮以求中者也。

translations.literal: Ancient sage kings all showed reverent sincerity and utmost honor toward ancestors and fathers, and only then could pure transformation flow through the four seas and hidden feeling reach the spirits — one should indeed examine abolition and establishment in ancient canon and seek the mean through feeling and ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient sage kings all showed reverent sincerity and utmost honor toward ancestors and fathers, and only then could pure transformation flow through the four seas and hidden feeling reach the spirits — one should indeed examine abolition and establishment in ancient canon and seek the mean through feeling and ritual.

sentences.zh: 禮，天子七廟，三昭三穆與太祖而七。

translations.literal: Ritual: the Son of Heaven has seven temples — three zhao three mu with the Grand Ancestor making seven.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual: the Son of Heaven has seven temples — three zhao three mu with the Grand Ancestor making seven.

sentences.zh: 自考廟以至祖考五廟，皆月祭之。

translations.literal: From the temple of self-examination to the five temples of ancestors and fathers, all receive monthly sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: From the temple of self-examination to the five temples of ancestors and fathers, all receive monthly sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 遠廟為祧，有二祧，享嘗乃止。

translations.literal: The distant temple becomes tiao; there are two tiao; offering and tasting then cease.
translations.idiomatic: The distant temple becomes tiao; there are two tiao; offering and tasting then cease.

sentences.zh: 去祧為壇，去壇為墠，有禱然後祭之，此宗廟之次、親疏之序也。

translations.literal: Beyond tiao is the altar; beyond the altar is the open ground; when there is prayer then sacrifice is made — this is the order of ancestral temples and the sequence of near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond tiao is the altar; beyond the altar is the open ground; when there is prayer then sacrifice is made — this is the order of ancestral temples and the sequence of near and far.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄以為祧者文王武王之廟，王肅以為五世六世之祖。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan held that tiao were the temples of King Wen and King Wu; Wang Su held they were ancestors of the fifth and sixth generations.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan held that tiao were the temples of King Wen and King Wu; Wang Su held they were ancestors of the fifth and sixth generations.

sentences.zh: 尋去祧之言，則祧非文、武之廟矣。

translations.literal: Examining the words "beyond tiao," then tiao are not the temples of Wen and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the words "beyond tiao," then tiao are not the temples of Wen and Wu.

sentences.zh: 文、武，周之祖宗，何雲去祧為壇乎？

translations.literal: Wen and Wu were Zhou's ancestors — how can one speak of beyond tiao as altar?
translations.idiomatic: Wen and Wu were Zhou's ancestors — how can one speak of beyond tiao as altar?

sentences.zh: 明遠廟為祧者，無服之祖也。

translations.literal: Clearly the distant temple that becomes tiao is the ancestor beyond mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Clearly the distant temple that becomes tiao is the ancestor beyond mourning.

sentences.zh: 又遠廟則有享嘗之降，去祧則有壇墠之殊，明世遠者其義彌疏也。

translations.literal: Again for distant temples there is the descent of offering and tasting; beyond tiao there is the difference of altar and open ground — clearly the more distant the generation the more sparse the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Again for distant temples there is the descent of offering and tasting; beyond tiao there is the difference of altar and open ground — clearly the more distant the generation the more sparse the meaning.

sentences.zh: 若祧是文、武之廟，宜同月祭于太祖，雖推後稷以配天，由功德之所始，非尊崇之義每有差降也。

translations.literal: If tiao were the temples of Wen and Wu they should like the Grand Ancestor receive monthly sacrifice; though Houji is elevated to match Heaven, that is from the beginning of merit, not that the meaning of honor has difference and descent each time.
translations.idiomatic: If tiao were the temples of Wen and Wu they should like the Grand Ancestor receive monthly sacrifice; though Houji is elevated to match Heaven, that is from the beginning of merit, not that the meaning of honor has difference and descent each time.

sentences.zh: 又禮有以多為貴者，故傳稱「德厚者流光，德薄者流卑「。

translations.literal: Again ritual has what values the many; therefore tradition says, "Thick virtue shines far; thin virtue flows low."
translations.idiomatic: Again ritual has what values the many; therefore tradition says, "Thick virtue shines far; thin virtue flows low."

sentences.zh: 又言自上以下降殺以兩，禮也。

translations.literal: Again it says from above to below reduction by twos — that is ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Again it says from above to below reduction by twos — that is ritual.

sentences.zh: 此則尊卑等級之典，上下殊異之文。

translations.literal: This is the canon of honor and lowliness, the text of difference above and below.
translations.idiomatic: This is the canon of honor and lowliness, the text of difference above and below.

sentences.zh: 而雲天子諸侯俱祭五廟，何哉？

translations.literal: Yet it says Son of Heaven and feudal lords alike sacrifice at five temples — why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet it says Son of Heaven and feudal lords alike sacrifice at five temples — why?

sentences.zh: 又王祭嫡殤，下及來孫。

translations.literal: Again the king sacrifices for legitimate early-dead sons, extending down to coming generations.
translations.idiomatic: Again the king sacrifices for legitimate early-dead sons, extending down to coming generations.

sentences.zh: 而上祀之禮不過高祖。

translations.literal: Yet sacrifice by superiors does not exceed the High Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet sacrifice by superiors does not exceed the High Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 推隆恩於下流，替誠敬於尊廟，亦非聖人制禮之意也。

translations.literal: Pushing honor down the stream while replacing sincere reverence at the honored temple — this too is not the sage's intent in making ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Pushing honor down the stream while replacing sincere reverence at the honored temple — this too is not the sage's intent in making ritual.

sentences.zh: 是以泰始建廟，從王氏議，以禮父為士，子為天子諸侯，祭以天子諸侯，其屍服以士服。

translations.literal: Therefore when Taishi established the temple they followed the Wang clan's argument: by ritual the father is a knight and the son Son of Heaven or feudal lord, yet sacrifice uses Son of Heaven and feudal lord while the corpse's garment uses knight's garment.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when Taishi established the temple they followed the Wang clan's argument: by ritual the father is a knight and the son Son of Heaven or feudal lord, yet sacrifice uses Son of Heaven and feudal lord while the corpse's garment uses knight's garment.

sentences.zh: 故上及征西，以備六世之數。

translations.literal: Thus upstream to Pacifying the West, to complete the number of six generations.
translations.idiomatic: Thus upstream to Pacifying the West, to complete the number of six generations.

sentences.zh: 宣皇雖為太祖，尚在子孫之位，至於殷祭之日，未申東向之禮，所謂子雖齊聖，不先父食者矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan though Grand Ancestor was still in the place of descendants; on the day of the great offering he had not yet received the east-facing rite — what is called though the son equals sainthood he does not eat before the father.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan though Grand Ancestor was still in the place of descendants; on the day of the great offering he had not yet received the east-facing rite — what is called though the son equals sainthood he does not eat before the father.

sentences.zh: 今京兆以上既遷，太祖始得居正，議者以昭穆未足，欲屈太祖于卑坐，臣以為非禮典之旨也。

translations.literal: Now that Jingzhao and above have moved, the Grand Ancestor at last occupies the correct place; debaters, because zhao and mu are not full, wish to bend the Grand Ancestor to the low seat — your servant holds this is not the intent of ritual canon.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Jingzhao and above have moved, the Grand Ancestor at last occupies the correct place; debaters, because zhao and mu are not full, wish to bend the Grand Ancestor to the low seat — your servant holds this is not the intent of ritual canon.

sentences.zh: 所謂與太祖而七，自是昭穆既足，太廟在六世之外，非為須滿七廟乃得居太祖也。

translations.literal: What is called "with the Grand Ancestor making seven" is itself that zhao and mu are already full and the Grand Temple lies outside the six generations — not that one must fill seven temples before the Grand Ancestor may occupy that place.
translations.idiomatic: What is called "with the Grand Ancestor making seven" is itself that zhao and mu are already full and the Grand Temple lies outside the six generations — not that one must fill seven temples before the Grand Ancestor may occupy that place.

sentences.zh: 議者又以四府君神主，宜永同于殷祫。

translations.literal: Debaters also held the spirit tablets of the four lords should forever share the great offering like the yin sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Debaters also held the spirit tablets of the four lords should forever share the great offering like the yin sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 臣又以為不然。

translations.literal: Your servant again holds this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant again holds this is not so.

sentences.zh: 傳所謂毀廟之主，陳乎太祖，謂太祖以下先君之主也。

translations.literal: Tradition speaks of the destroyed temple's tablet displayed before the Grand Ancestor — meaning the tablets of former lords below the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition speaks of the destroyed temple's tablet displayed before the Grand Ancestor — meaning the tablets of former lords below the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 故白虎通云：「禘祫祭遷廟者，以其繼君之體，持其統而不絕也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Baihu Tong says, "The di and ha sacrifices move destroyed temples because they continue the lord's body and hold the line without breaking.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Baihu Tong says, "The di and ha sacrifices move destroyed temples because they continue the lord's body and hold the line without breaking.

sentences.zh: 」豈如四府君在太祖之前乎，非繼統之主，無靈命之瑞，非王業之基。

translations.literal: How could the four lords be before the Grand Ancestor? They are not lords who continue the line, have no auspicious mandate, are not the foundation of royal enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: How could the four lords be before the Grand Ancestor? They are not lords who continue the line, have no auspicious mandate, are not the foundation of royal enterprise.

sentences.zh: 昔以世近而及，今則情禮已遠，而當長饗殷祫，永虛太祖之位，求之禮籍。

translations.literal: Formerly because the generation was near they were included; now feeling and ritual are already far — yet they should long enjoy the great yin offering and forever leave the Grand Ancestor's place empty; seeking this in ritual texts —
translations.idiomatic: Formerly because the generation was near they were included; now feeling and ritual are already far — yet they should long enjoy the great yin offering and forever leave the Grand Ancestor's place empty; seeking this in ritual texts —

sentences.zh: 未見其可。

translations.literal: one does not see that it may be done.
translations.idiomatic: one does not see that it may be done.

sentences.zh: 昔永和之初，大議斯禮，于時虞喜、范宣並以洪儒碩學，咸謂四府君神主無緣永存於百世。

translations.literal: Formerly at the beginning of Yonghe there was great debate on this ritual; at that time Yu Xi and Fan Xuan, both great Confucian scholars, all held the four lords' spirit tablets had no reason to remain forever for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly at the beginning of Yonghe there was great debate on this ritual; at that time Yu Xi and Fan Xuan, both great Confucian scholars, all held the four lords' spirit tablets had no reason to remain forever for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 或欲瘞之兩階，或欲藏之石室，或欲為之改築，雖所執小異，而大歸是同。

translations.literal: Some wished to bury them at the two steps, some to store them in a stone chamber, some to rebuild for them — though what they held differed in small ways the great direction was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Some wished to bury them at the two steps, some to store them in a stone chamber, some to rebuild for them — though what they held differed in small ways the great direction was the same.

sentences.zh: 若宣皇既居群廟之上，而四主禘祫不已，則大晉殷祭長無太祖之位矣。

translations.literal: If Emperor Xuan already stands above the group of temples and the four lords' di and ha offerings never cease, then Great Jin's great yin sacrifice would forever lack the Grand Ancestor's place.
translations.idiomatic: If Emperor Xuan already stands above the group of temples and the four lords' di and ha offerings never cease, then Great Jin's great yin sacrifice would forever lack the Grand Ancestor's place.

sentences.zh: 夫理貴有中，不必過厚，禮與世遷，豈可順而不斷？

translations.literal: Principle values the mean — one need not exceed in thickness; ritual moves with the age — how can one follow without deciding?
translations.idiomatic: Principle values the mean — one need not exceed in thickness; ritual moves with the age — how can one follow without deciding?

sentences.zh: 故臣子之情雖篤，而靈、厲之諡彌彰，追遠之懷雖切，而遷毀之禮為用。

translations.literal: Thus though ministers' and sons' feeling is deep, the posthumous titles of Ling and Li grow ever clearer; though longing for the distant is keen, the ritual of transfer and destruction is what applies.
translations.idiomatic: Thus though ministers' and sons' feeling is deep, the posthumous titles of Ling and Li grow ever clearer; though longing for the distant is keen, the ritual of transfer and destruction is what applies.

sentences.zh: 豈不有心于加厚，顧禮制不可踰耳。

translations.literal: Is it not that the heart wishes to add thickness but ritual system cannot be overstepped?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not that the heart wishes to add thickness but ritual system cannot be overstepped?

sentences.zh: 石室則藏於廟北，改築則未知所處。

translations.literal: Stone chamber means storing north of the temple; rebuilding means not knowing where to place them.
translations.idiomatic: Stone chamber means storing north of the temple; rebuilding means not knowing where to place them.

sentences.zh: 虞主所以依神，神移則有瘞埋之禮。

translations.literal: The yu tablet exists to rely on the spirit; when the spirit moves there is the ritual of burial.
translations.idiomatic: The yu tablet exists to rely on the spirit; when the spirit moves there is the ritual of burial.

sentences.zh: 四主若饗祀宜廢，亦神之所不依也。

translations.literal: If the four lords' offering sacrifice should be abolished, that too is what the spirit does not rely on.
translations.idiomatic: If the four lords' offering sacrifice should be abolished, that too is what the spirit does not rely on.

sentences.zh: 准傍事例，宜同虞主之瘞埋。

translations.literal: Following parallel cases one should like the yu tablet's burial.
translations.idiomatic: Following parallel cases one should like the yu tablet's burial.

sentences.zh: 然經典難詳，群言錯繆，非臣淺識所能折中。

translations.literal: Yet the classics are hard to detail and many words err — this is not what your servant's shallow understanding can reconcile.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the classics are hard to detail and many words err — this is not what your servant's shallow understanding can reconcile.

sentences.zh: 時學者多從燾議，竟未施行。

translations.literal: At that time most scholars followed Dao's argument; in the end it was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: At that time most scholars followed Dao's argument; in the end it was not implemented.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝受命，拜太常。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song received the Mandate he was appointed Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Song received the Mandate he was appointed Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 雖外戚貴顯，而彌自沖約。

translations.literal: Though an honored imperial in-law he was all the more self-restrained and modest.
translations.idiomatic: Though an honored imperial in-law he was all the more self-restrained and modest.

sentences.zh: 茅屋蔬飧，不改其舊。

translations.literal: Thatched hut and vegetable meal — he did not change the old ways.
translations.idiomatic: Thatched hut and vegetable meal — he did not change the old ways.

sentences.zh: 所得奉祿，與親戚共之。

translations.literal: The salary he received he shared with kin.
translations.idiomatic: The salary he received he shared with kin.

sentences.zh: 永初三年致事，拜光祿大夫，加金章紫綬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu he retired from affairs and was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with gold seal and purple ribbon added.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchu's third year he retired from affairs and was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with gold seal and purple ribbon added.

sentences.zh: 卒，少帝贈左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When he died Emperor Shao posthumously gave him Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When he died Emperor Shao posthumously gave him Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 長子邃，宜都太守。

translations.literal: His eldest son Sui was Administrator of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Sui was administrator of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 邃子凝之，學涉有當世才，與司空徐湛之為異常交。

translations.literal: Sui's son Ningzhi, learned and with talent for the age, had an unusual friendship with Minister of Works Xu Zhanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Sui's son Ningzhi, learned and with talent for the age, had an unusual friendship with Minister of Works Xu Zhanzhi.

sentences.zh: 年少時，與傅僧佑俱以通家子，始為文帝所引見。

translations.literal: In youth he and Fu Sengyou, both sons of connected houses, were first received in audience by Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he and Fu Sengyou, both sons of connected houses, were first received in audience by Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 時上與何尚之論鑄錢事，凝之便幹其語次，上因回與語。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor was discussing coinage with He Shangzhi; Ningzhi inserted himself into the thread of his words; the Emperor therefore turned and spoke with him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor was discussing coinage with He Shangzhi; Ningzhi inserted himself into the thread of his words; the emperor therefore turned and spoke with him.

sentences.zh: 僧佑引凝之衣令止，凝之大言曰：「明主難再遇，便應政盡所懷。

translations.literal: Sengyou pulled Ningzhi's robe to make him stop; Ningzhi spoke loudly, "A bright lord is hard to meet twice — one should at once exhaust what is in the breast.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyou pulled Ningzhi's robe to make him stop; Ningzhi spoke loudly, "A bright lord is hard to meet twice — one should at once exhaust what is in the breast.

sentences.zh: 」上與往復十餘反，凝之辭韻詮序，上甚賞焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor went back and forth more than ten exchanges; Ningzhi's wording and tone were orderly and complete; the Emperor greatly admired him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went back and forth more than ten exchanges; Ningzhi's wording and tone were orderly and complete; the emperor greatly admired him.

sentences.zh: 後為尚書左丞，以徐湛之党，為元凶所殺。

translations.literal: Later he was Left Assistant Minister of the Secretariat; as a member of Xu Zhanzhi's faction he was killed by the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was left assistant minister of the secretariat; as a member of Xu Zhanzhi's faction he was killed by the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 凝之子寅字士若，事在沈攸之傳。

translations.literal: Ningzhi's son Yin, styled Shiruo — his affairs are in the biography of Shen Youzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzhi's son Yin, courtesy name Shiruo — his affairs are in the biography of Shen Youzhi.

sentences.zh: 寅弟棱，後軍參軍。

translations.literal: Yin's younger brother Leng served as staff officer to the Rear Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's younger brother Leng served as staff officer to the rear army.

sentences.zh: 棱子嚴。

translations.literal: Leng's son Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Leng's son Yan.

sentences.zh: 嚴字彥威，幼有孝性，居父憂以毀聞。

translations.literal: Yan, styled Yanwei, had filial nature from youth; in mourning for his father he was famed for grief-wasting.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, courtesy name Yanwei, had filial nature from youth; in mourning for his father he was famed for grief-wasting.

sentences.zh: 孤貧勤學，行止書卷不離手。

translations.literal: Orphaned and poor he studied diligently; going and stopping he never left books from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor he studied diligently; going and stopping he never left books from his hand.

sentences.zh: 從叔未甄為江夏郡，攜嚴之官，於途作屯遊賦，又作七算，辭並典麗。

translations.literal: His father's younger cousin Wei Zhen was in Jiangxia Commandery and took Yan to office; on the road he composed the Fu of Encampment Travel and also the Seven Calculations — both texts classical and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: His father's younger cousin Wei Zhen was in Jiangxia commandery and took Yan to office; on the road he composed the Fu of Encampment Travel and also the Seven Calculations — both texts classical and elegant.

sentences.zh: 性孤介，未嘗造請。

translations.literal: By nature solitary and upright, he never made calls on others.
translations.idiomatic: By nature solitary and upright, he never made calls on others.

sentences.zh: 梁僕射徐勉欲識之，嚴終不詣。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Works Xu Mian wished to know him; Yan in the end never went to him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Works Xu Mian wished to know him; Yan in the end never went to him.

sentences.zh: 累遷湘東王宣惠輕車府參軍兼記室。

translations.literal: Promoted repeatedly to Staff Officer of the Light Chariot Office under Prince Xuanhui of Eastern Xiang and Concurrent Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted repeatedly to staff officer of the light chariot office under Prince Xuanhui of Eastern Xiang and concurrent recorder.

sentences.zh: 嚴於學多所諳記，尤精漢書，諷誦略皆上口。

translations.literal: Yan in learning knew much by heart and especially mastered the Han Shu; reciting it he could mostly speak it from memory.
translations.idiomatic: Yan in learning knew much by heart and especially mastered the Han Shu; reciting it he could mostly speak it from memory.

sentences.zh: 王嘗自執四部書目試之，嚴自甲至丁卷中各對一事，並作者姓名，遂無遺失。

translations.literal: The Prince once himself held the catalogue of the four sections to test him; from scroll A to D Yan answered one item in each about the author — none was missed.
translations.idiomatic: The prince once himself held the catalogue of the four sections to test him; from scroll A to D Yan answered one item in each about the author — none was missed.

sentences.zh: 王遷荊州，隨府轉西中郎安西錄事參軍，曆義陽、武寧郡守。

translations.literal: When the Prince moved to Jing Province Yan followed the headquarters to Western Central Administrator and Recorder of the Pacifying West, and served successively as Administrator of Yiyang and Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince moved to Jing Province Yan followed the headquarters to western central administrator and recorder of the Pacifying West, and served successively as administrator of Yiyang and Wuning.

sentences.zh: 郡界蠻左，前郡守常選武人以兵鎮之，嚴獨以數門生單車入境，群蠻悅服。

translations.literal: Within the commandery were Man on the left; former administrators always chose martial men with troops to garrison them; Yan alone with a few disciples and a single cart entered the territory and the Man tribes submitted gladly.
translations.idiomatic: Within the commandery were Man on the left; former administrators always chose martial men with troops to garrison them; Yan alone with a few disciples and a single cart entered the territory and the Man tribes submitted gladly.

sentences.zh: 後卒于鎮南諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Later he died as Consultant of Pacifying the South.
translations.idiomatic: Later he died as consultant of Pacifying the South.

sentences.zh: 文集十卷。

translations.literal: Collected writings in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Collected writings in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 嚴族叔未甄，燾曾孫也。

translations.literal: Yan's clan uncle Wei Zhen was Dao's great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's clan uncle Wei Zhen was Dao's great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 父潭之，左戶尚書。

translations.literal: His father Tanzhi was Minister of the Left Household.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tanzhi was minister of the left household.

sentences.zh: 未甄有才幹，少為外兄汝南周顒所知，仕梁為太尉長史。

translations.literal: Wei Zhen had talent and ability; in youth he was known to his maternal uncle Zhou Yong of Runan; serving Liang he was Chief Secretary to the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhen had talent and ability; in youth he was known to his maternal uncle Zhou Yong of Runan; serving Liang he was chief secretary to the grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 丁所生母憂，三年廬於墓側。

translations.literal: On the death of the mother who bore him he observed mourning three years in a hut at the tomb side.
translations.idiomatic: On the death of the mother who bore him he observed mourning three years in a hut at the tomb side.

sentences.zh: 曆廷尉卿，江夏太守，卒。

translations.literal: He served successively as Director of Punishments and Administrator of Jiangxia, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as director of punishments and administrator of Jiangxia, then died.

sentences.zh: 子盾。

translations.literal: His son Dun.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dun.

sentences.zh: 盾字宣卿，幼從征士琅邪諸葛璩受五經。

translations.literal: Dun, styled Xuanqing, in youth followed the recluse Zhuge Ju of Langye in the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Dun, courtesy name Xuanqing, in youth followed the recluse Zhuge Ju of Langye in the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 璩學徒常有數十百人，盾處其間，無所狎比。

translations.literal: Ju's disciples often numbered several tens or hundreds; Dun among them was intimate with none.
translations.idiomatic: Ju's disciples often numbered several tens or hundreds; Dun among them was intimate with none.

sentences.zh: 璩曰：「此生王佐才也。

translations.literal: Ju said, "This student has the talent of a king's assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Ju said, "This student has the talent of a king's assistant.

sentences.zh: 」為尚書中兵郎。

translations.literal: He served as Gentleman of the Central Army Section of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served as gentleman of the central army section of the ministry of revenue.

sentences.zh: 美風姿，善容止，每趨奏，梁武帝甚悅焉。

translations.literal: Fine in bearing and graceful in deportment, each time he hurried to audience Emperor Wu of Liang was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Fine in bearing and graceful in deportment, each time he hurried to audience Emperor Wu of Liang was very pleased.

sentences.zh: 入兼中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: He entered concurrently as Secretariat Gentleman for Current Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He entered concurrently as secretariat gentleman for current affairs.

sentences.zh: 盾有孝性，嘗隨父宿直廷尉府，母劉氏在宅夜暴亡，盾左手中指忽痛不得寢。

translations.literal: Dun had filial nature; once he followed his father on overnight duty at the Directorate of Punishments; his mother Liu at home suddenly died at night; Dun's middle finger on his left hand suddenly ached and he could not sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Dun had filial nature; once he followed his father on overnight duty at the directorate of punishments; his mother Liu at home suddenly died at night; Dun's middle finger on his left hand suddenly ached and he could not sleep.

sentences.zh: 及旦，宅信果報凶問，其感通如此。

translations.literal: At dawn a messenger from home indeed brought word of death — such was his spiritual connection.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn a messenger from home indeed brought word of death — such was his spiritual connection.

sentences.zh: 服未終，父卒，居喪五年，不出廬戶，形骸枯悴，家人不識。

translations.literal: Before mourning ended his father died; he observed mourning five years without leaving the hut gate; his form withered until kin did not recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: Before mourning ended his father died; he observed mourning five years without leaving the hut gate; his form withered until kin did not recognize him.

sentences.zh: 武帝累敕抑譬。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu repeatedly sent edicts to restrain and comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu repeatedly sent edicts to restrain and comfort him.

sentences.zh: 後累遷御史中丞，性公強，甚稱職。

translations.literal: Later promoted repeatedly to Imperial Censor; by nature fair and strong, he was very fit for the office.
translations.idiomatic: Later promoted repeatedly to imperial censor; by nature fair and strong, he was very fit for the office.

sentences.zh: 中大通五年，帝幸同泰寺開講，設四部大會，眾數萬人。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhongdatong the Emperor visited Tongtai Temple to open lectures and set the four-section great assembly; the crowd numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongdatong's fifth year the emperor visited Tongtai Temple to open lectures and set the four-section great assembly; the crowd numbered tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 南越所獻馴象忽於眾中狂逸，眾皆駭散，唯盾與散騎侍郎裴之禮嶷然自若，帝甚嘉焉。

translations.literal: A tame elephant presented by Southern Yue suddenly ran wild among the crowd; all were terrified and scattered; only Dun and Regular Attendant Pei Zhili stood firm and calm; the Emperor greatly praised this.
translations.idiomatic: A tame elephant presented by Southern Yue suddenly ran wild among the crowd; all were terrified and scattered; only Dun and regular attendant Pei Zhili stood firm and calm; the emperor greatly praised this.

sentences.zh: 大同二年，為中領軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong he was Central Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong's second year he was central army commander.

sentences.zh: 領軍管天下兵要，監局事多，盾為人敏贍，有風力，長於撥繁，職事甚理。

translations.literal: The Central Army controlled the empire's military keys; supervisory office affairs were many; Dun as a man was quick and capable with force of character, skilled at untangling complexity — office affairs were very well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: The central army controlled the empire's military keys; supervisory office affairs were many; Dun as a man was quick and capable with force of character, skilled at untangling complexity — office affairs were very well ordered.

sentences.zh: 先是吳平侯蕭景居此職著聲，至是盾復繼之。

translations.literal: Earlier Marquis of Wu Ping Xiao Jing had held this post with renown; now Dun again followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Marquis of Wu Ping Xiao Jing had held this post with renown; now Dun again followed him.

sentences.zh: 後卒于領軍將軍，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: Later he died as General Who Commands the Army; posthumous title Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Later he died as general who commands the army; posthumous title Zhong.

sentences.zh: 盾弟厥字獻卿，亦以幹局稱。

translations.literal: Dun's younger brother Jue, styled Xianqing, was also famed for administrative capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's younger brother Jue, courtesy name Xianqing, was also famed for administrative capacity.

sentences.zh: 為晉安太守，郡居山海，常結聚逋逃，前二千石討捕不能止。

translations.literal: As Administrator of Jin'an the commandery lay among mountains and sea and often harbored fugitives; former administrators of two thousand households could not stop them by pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: As administrator of Jin'an the commandery lay among mountains and sea and often harbored fugitives; former administrators could not stop them by pursuit.

sentences.zh: 厥下車宣化，凶黨皆繈負而出，自是居人復業。

translations.literal: When Jue took office he proclaimed transformation; the violent bands all came out carrying children on their backs, and thereafter the residents returned to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: When Jue took office he proclaimed transformation; the violent bands all came out carrying children on their backs, and thereafter the residents returned to their occupations.

sentences.zh: 然政嚴，百姓謂之臧彪。

translations.literal: Yet his governance was strict; the people called him Zang Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his governance was strict; the people called him Zang Biao.

sentences.zh: 前後再兼中書通事舍人，卒于兼司農卿。

translations.literal: Before and after he twice served concurrently as Secretariat Gentleman for Current Affairs and died as Concurrent Director of the Imperial Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Before and after he twice served concurrently as secretariat gentleman for current affairs and died as concurrent director of the imperial granaries.

sentences.zh: 厥前後居職，所掌之局大事及蘭台廷尉所不能決者，敕並付厥。

translations.literal: In offices before and after, great affairs of the bureaus he controlled and what the Orchid Terrace and Directorate of Punishments could not decide were all by edict given to Jue.
translations.idiomatic: In offices before and after, great affairs of the bureaus he controlled and what the Orchid Terrace and directorate of punishments could not decide were all by edict given to Jue.

sentences.zh: 辯斷精明，咸得其理。

translations.literal: His judgment was penetrating and clear; all obtained their principle.
translations.idiomatic: His judgment was penetrating and clear; all obtained their principle.

sentences.zh: 卒後，有撾登聞鼓訴求付清直舍人，帝曰：「臧厥既亡，此事便無所付。

translations.literal: After his death someone beat the petition drum seeking assignment to the Clear and Straight Gentleman's office; the Emperor said, "Now that Zang Jue is dead, this matter has no one to assign.
translations.idiomatic: After his death someone beat the petition drum seeking assignment to the clear and straight gentleman's office; the emperor said, "Now that Zang Jue is dead, this matter has no one to assign.

sentences.zh: 」其見知如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 子操，尚書三公郎。

translations.literal: His son Cao held the post of Gentleman of the Three Offices Section.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cao held the post of gentleman of the three offices section.

sentences.zh: 熹字義和，燾之弟也，與燾並好經學。

translations.literal: Xi, styled Yihe, was Dao's younger brother; he and Dao both loved classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, courtesy name Yihe, was Dao's younger brother; he and Dao both loved classical learning.

sentences.zh: 隆安初兵起，熹乃習騎射，志立功名。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Long'an when troops rose Xi then practiced riding and shooting, intent on establishing merit.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Long'an when troops rose Xi then practiced riding and shooting, intent on establishing merit.

sentences.zh: 嘗與溧陽令阮崇獵，遇猛獸突圍，獵徒並散，熹射之，應弦而倒。

translations.literal: Once hunting with Liyang Magistrate Ruan Chong, a fierce beast broke the encirclement; the hunters all scattered; Xi shot it and it fell at the twang of the string.
translations.idiomatic: Once hunting with Liyang magistrate Ruan Chong, a fierce beast broke the encirclement; the hunters all scattered; Xi shot it and it fell at the twang of the string.

sentences.zh: 從宋武入京城，進至建鄴。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Wu into the capital region he advanced to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Following Emperor Wu into the capital region he advanced to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 桓玄走，武帝便使熹入宮收圖書器物，封府庫。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan fled the Emperor had Xi enter the palace to collect books, instruments, and goods and seal the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan fled the emperor had Xi enter the palace to collect books, instruments, and goods and seal the treasury.

sentences.zh: 有金飾樂器，武帝問熹：「卿欲此乎？

translations.literal: There were gold-decorated musical instruments; the Emperor asked Xi, "Do you want these?
translations.idiomatic: There were gold-decorated musical instruments; the emperor asked Xi, "Do you want these?

sentences.zh: 」熹正色曰：「主上幽逼，播越非所，將軍首建大義，劬勞王室，雖復不肖，實無情于樂。

translations.literal: Xi sternly said, "The lord above is confined and driven far — not where he should be; the general first raised great righteousness and toils for the royal house — though I am unworthy, I truly have no heart for music.
translations.idiomatic: Xi sternly said, "The lord above is confined and driven far — not where he should be; the general first raised great righteousness and toils for the royal house — though I am unworthy, I truly have no heart for music.

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「聊以戲耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and said, "I spoke in jest only.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "I spoke in jest only.

sentences.zh: 」以建義功，封始興縣五等侯，參武帝車騎、中軍軍事。

translations.literal: For merit in establishing righteousness he was enfeoffed Marquis of the Fifth Rank of Shixing and joined the Emperor's Chariots and Cavalry and Central Army staff.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in establishing righteousness he was enfeoffed fifth-rank marquis of Shixing and joined the emperor's chariots and cavalry and central army staff.

sentences.zh: 武帝將征廣固，議者多不同，熹贊成其行。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was about to campaign against Guanggu many debaters disagreed; Xi approved the undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to campaign against Guanggu many debaters disagreed; Xi approved the undertaking.

sentences.zh: 武帝遣朱齡石統大眾伐蜀，命熹奇兵出中水，領建平、巴東二郡太守。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Zhu Lingshi to command the great host against Shu and ordered Xi with a separate force out through Zhongshui, holding the two commanderies of Jianping and Badong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Zhu Lingshi to command the great host against Shu and ordered Xi with a separate force out through Zhongshui, holding the two commanderies of Jianping and Badong.

sentences.zh: 蜀主譙縱遣大將譙撫之屯牛脾，又遣譙小苟重兵塞打鼻。

translations.literal: Shu's lord Qiao Zong sent the great general Qiao Fuzhi to garrison Niupi and also sent Qiao Xiaogou with heavy troops to block Dabi.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's lord Qiao Zong sent the great general Qiao Fuzhi to garrison Niupi and also sent Qiao Xiaogou with heavy troops to block Dabi.

sentences.zh: 熹至牛脾，撫之敗走，追斬之，成都平。

translations.literal: When Xi reached Niupi Fuzhi was defeated and fled; Xi pursued and beheaded him; Chengdu was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi reached Niupi Fuzhi was defeated and fled; Xi pursued and beheaded him; Chengdu was pacified.

sentences.zh: 熹遇疾卒於蜀，追贈光祿勳。

translations.literal: Xi fell ill and died in Shu; posthumously he was given Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Xi fell ill and died in Shu; posthumously he was given Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 子質字含文，少好鷹犬，善蒱博意錢之戲。

translations.literal: His son Zhi, styled Hanwen, from youth loved hawks and dogs and was skilled at cockfighting and pitch-pot games.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi, courtesy name Hanwen, from youth loved hawks and dogs and was skilled at cockfighting and pitch-pot games.

sentences.zh: 長六尺七寸，出面露口，頹頂拳發。

translations.literal: He stood six feet seven inches; his face protruded and mouth showed; crown receded and hair curled.
translations.idiomatic: He stood six feet seven inches; his face protruded and mouth showed; crown receded and hair curled.

sentences.zh: 初為世子中軍參軍，嘗詣護軍趙倫之，倫之名位已重，不相接。

translations.literal: At first he was staff officer to the Heir Apparent's Central Army; once he called on Protector of the Army Zhao Lunzhi; Lunzhi's name and rank were already weighty and he did not receive him.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was staff officer to the heir apparent's central army; once he called on Protector of the Army Zhao Lunzhi; Lunzhi's name and rank were already weighty and he did not receive him.

sentences.zh: 質憤然起曰：「大丈夫各以老嫗作門戶，何至以此中相輕。

translations.literal: Zhi angrily rose and said, "Great men each make an old matron their gate — why go so far as to look down on one in the middle?
translations.idiomatic: Zhi angrily rose and said, "Great men each make an old matron their gate — why go so far as to look down on one in the middle?

sentences.zh: 」倫之慚謝，質拂衣而去。

translations.literal: Lunzhi ashamed apologized; Zhi shook out his robe and left.
translations.idiomatic: Lunzhi ashamed apologized; Zhi shook out his robe and left.

sentences.zh: 後為江夏王義恭撫軍參軍，以輕薄無檢，為文帝所嫌，徙給事中。

translations.literal: Later he was staff officer to Prince Jiangxia Yigong's Pacifying Army; for being frivolous and unrestrained he was disliked by Emperor Wen and was transferred to Supervising Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was staff officer to Prince Jiangxia Yigong's pacifying army; for being frivolous and unrestrained he was disliked by Emperor Wen and was transferred to supervising master of writing.

sentences.zh: 會稽長公主每為之言，乃出為建平太守，甚得蠻楚心。

translations.literal: The Princess of Kuaiji often spoke for him; he was then sent out as Administrator of Jianping and greatly won the hearts of the Man and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Kuaiji often spoke for him; he was then sent out as administrator of Jianping and greatly won the hearts of the Man and Chu.

sentences.zh: 曆竟陵內史，巴東建平二郡太守，吏人便之。

translations.literal: He served successively as Interior Minister of Jingling and Administrator of Badong and Jianping; officials and people found him easy.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as interior minister of Jingling and administrator of Badong and Jianping; officials and people found him easy.

sentences.zh: 質年始出三十，屢居名郡，涉獵文史，尺牘便敏，有氣幹，好言兵。

translations.literal: Zhi had just passed thirty and repeatedly held famous commanderies; he ranged through literature and history; letters and documents came easily; he had spirit and capacity and loved speaking of war.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had just passed thirty and repeatedly held famous commanderies; he ranged through literature and history; letters and documents came easily; he had spirit and capacity and loved speaking of war.

sentences.zh: 文帝謂可大任，以為徐、兗二州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen thought he could bear great responsibility and made him Governor of Xu and Yan with added command.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen thought he could bear great responsibility and made him governor of Xu and Yan with added command.

sentences.zh: 在鎮奢費，爵命無章，為有司所糾。

translations.literal: In his post he was extravagant; enfeoffments and appointments were without rule; he was impeached by the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: In his post he was extravagant; enfeoffments and appointments were without rule; he was impeached by the responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 遇赦。

translations.literal: He met amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: He met amnesty.

sentences.zh: 與范曄、徐湛之等厚善。

translations.literal: He was on close terms with Fan Ye and Xu Zhanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He was on close terms with Fan Ye and Xu Zhanzhi.

sentences.zh: 曄謀反，量質必與之同。

translations.literal: When Ye plotted rebellion he reckoned Zhi would surely join him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ye plotted rebellion he reckoned Zhi would surely join him.

sentences.zh: 會事發，復為義興太守。

translations.literal: When the affair broke out he again became Administrator of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair broke out he again became administrator of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，遷南譙王義宣司空司馬、南平內史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was transferred to Prince Nanqiao Yixuan's Staff Officer to the Minister of Works and Interior Minister of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he was transferred to Prince Nanqiao Yixuan's staff officer to the minister of works and interior minister of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 未之職，會魏太武帝圍汝南，戍主陳憲固守告急，文帝遣質輕往壽陽，與安蠻司馬劉康祖等救憲。

translations.literal: Before taking office, when Wei Emperor Taiwu besieged Runan the garrison commander Chen Xian held firm and reported urgency; Emperor Wen sent Zhi lightly to Shouyang to rescue Xian together with Pacifying Man Staff Officer Liu Kangzu and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Before taking office, when Wei Emperor Taiwu besieged Runan the garrison commander Chen Xian held firm and reported urgency; Emperor Wen sent Zhi lightly to Shouyang to rescue Xian together with pacifying man staff officer Liu Kangzu and the rest.

sentences.zh: 後太武率大眾數十萬向彭城，以質為輔國將軍北救。

translations.literal: Later Taiwu led a great host of several hundred thousand toward Pengcheng and Zhi was made Auxiliary-state General for northern relief.
translations.idiomatic: Later Taiwu led a great host of several hundred thousand toward Pengcheng and Zhi was made auxiliary-state general for northern relief.

sentences.zh: 始至盱眙，太武已過淮。

translations.literal: Just reaching Xuyi, Taiwu had already crossed the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Just reaching Xuyi, Taiwu had already crossed the Huai.

sentences.zh: 二十八年正月，太武自廣陵北返，悉力攻盱眙，就質求酒。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-eighth year Taiwu returned north from Guangling and used full force to attack Xuyi; he asked Zhi for wine.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-eighth year Taiwu returned north from Guangling and used full force to attack Xuyi; he asked Zhi for wine.

sentences.zh: 質封溲便與之，太武怒甚，築長圍一夜便合。

translations.literal: Zhi sealed urine and feces and sent them; Taiwu was furious beyond measure and built a long encirclement that joined in one night.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi sealed urine and feces and sent them; Taiwu was furious beyond measure and built a long encirclement that joined in one night.

sentences.zh: 質報太武書云：「爾不聞童謠言邪？

translations.literal: Zhi replied to Taiwu's letter, "Have you not heard what the children's rhyme says?
translations.idiomatic: Zhi replied to Taiwu's letter, "Have you not heard what the children's rhyme says?

sentences.zh: 虜馬飲江水，佛狸死卯年。

translations.literal: Barbarian horses drink river water; Foluo dies in the mao year.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian horses drink river water; Foluo dies in the mao year.

sentences.zh: 冥期使然，非復人事。

translations.literal: Dark fate makes it so — no longer a matter of human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Dark fate makes it so — no longer a matter of human affairs.

sentences.zh: 寡人受命相滅，期之白登，師行未遠，爾自送死，豈容復令爾饗有桑幹哉。

translations.literal: I received the mandate to destroy you; the term is set at Baideng; the army has not gone far and you yourself come to die — how can I again let you feast on Sanggan?
translations.idiomatic: I received the mandate to destroy you; the term is set at Baideng; the army has not gone far and you yourself come to die — how can I again let you feast on Sanggan?

sentences.zh: 假令寡人不能殺爾，爾由我而死。

translations.literal: Suppose I cannot kill you — you will die by me.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose I cannot kill you — you will die by me.

sentences.zh: 爾若有幸，得為亂兵所殺；

translations.literal: If you are lucky you will be killed by mutinous troops;
translations.idiomatic: If you are lucky you will be killed by mutinous troops;

sentences.zh: 爾若不幸，則生相鎖縛，載以一驢，負送都市。

translations.literal: if you are unlucky you will live chained and bound, carried on one donkey and sent to the capital market.
translations.idiomatic: if you are unlucky you will live chained and bound, carried on one donkey and sent to the capital market.

sentences.zh: 爾識智及眾，豈能勝苻堅邪？

translations.literal: You know wisdom and the multitude — can you surpass Fu Jian?
translations.idiomatic: You know wisdom and the multitude — can you surpass Fu Jian?

sentences.zh: 頃年展爾陸梁者，是爾未飲江太歲未卯故耳。

translations.literal: In recent years you spread your insolence only because you had not yet drunk the river and the Grand Year had not reached mao.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years you spread your insolence only because you had not yet drunk the river and the Grand Year had not reached mao.

sentences.zh: 」時魏地童謠曰：「軺車北來如穿雉，不意虜馬飲江水。

translations.literal: At that time a children's rhyme in Wei territory said, "The light carriage comes north like piercing a pheasant — who expected barbarian horses to drink river water.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a children's rhyme in Wei territory said, "The light carriage comes north like piercing a pheasant — who expected barbarian horses to drink river water.

sentences.zh: 虜主北歸石濟死，虜欲度江天不徙。

translations.literal: The barbarian lord returns north and dies at Shiji; the barbarian wishes to cross the river but Heaven will not shift.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian lord returns north and dies at Shiji; the barbarian wishes to cross the river but Heaven will not shift.

sentences.zh: 」故答書引之。

translations.literal: Therefore the reply letter cited it.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the reply letter cited it.

sentences.zh: 太武大怒，乃作鐵床，于上施鐵鑱，云：「破城得質，當坐之此上」。

translations.literal: Taiwu was greatly enraged and made an iron bed with iron spikes on it, saying, "When the city is taken and Zhi is obtained he shall sit on this.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu was greatly enraged and made an iron bed with iron spikes on it, saying, "When the city is taken and Zhi is obtained he shall sit on this.

sentences.zh: 質又與魏軍書，寫台格購斬太武封萬戶侯，賜布絹各萬疋。

translations.literal: Zhi also wrote to the Wei army, copying the court's posted reward for beheading Taiwu — enfeoffment as Marquis of Ten Thousand Households and ten thousand bolts each of cloth and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi also wrote to the Wei army, copying the court's posted reward for beheading Taiwu — enfeoffment as marquis of ten thousand households and ten thousand bolts each of cloth and silk.

sentences.zh: 魏以鉤車鉤垣樓，城內系絙，數百人叫呼引之，車不能退。

translations.literal: Wei used hook-carts to hook the tower ramparts; inside the city ropes were tied and several hundred men shouted and pulled — the carts could not retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Wei used hook-carts to hook the tower ramparts; inside the city ropes were tied and several hundred men shouted and pulled — the carts could not retreat.

sentences.zh: 質夜以木桶盛人，縣出城外，截其鉤獲之。

translations.literal: Zhi at night used wooden buckets holding men, hung them outside the wall, cut off the hooks and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi at night used wooden buckets holding men, hung them outside the wall, cut off the hooks and captured them.

sentences.zh: 明日又以沖車攻城，土堅密，每至，頹落下不過數斗。

translations.literal: The next day they again used battering rams against the wall; the earth was firm and dense — each time only several pecks fell.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they again used battering rams against the wall; the earth was firm and dense — each time only several pecks fell.

sentences.zh: 魏軍乃肉薄登城，墜而復升，莫有退者。

translations.literal: The Wei army then pressed flesh against the wall to climb; falling they climbed again — none retreated.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army then pressed flesh against the wall to climb; falling they climbed again — none retreated.

sentences.zh: 殺傷萬計，死者與城平。

translations.literal: Killed and wounded numbered in the tens of thousands; the dead were level with the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Killed and wounded numbered in the tens of thousands; the dead were level with the wall.

sentences.zh: 如此三旬，死者過半，太武乃解圍而歸。

translations.literal: Thus for thirty days; the dead exceeded half; Taiwu then lifted the siege and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Thus for thirty days; the dead exceeded half; Taiwu then lifted the siege and returned.

sentences.zh: 上嘉質功，以為甯蠻校尉、雍州刺史、監四州諸軍事。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised Zhi's merit and made him Colonel of Pacifying the Man, Governor of Yong, and overseer of four provinces' military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Zhi's merit and made him colonel of pacifying the man, governor of Yong, and overseer of four provinces' military affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年，文帝又北侵，使質率見力向潼關。

translations.literal: The next year Emperor Wen again invaded north and ordered Zhi to lead available troops toward Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Emperor Wen again invaded north and ordered Zhi to lead available troops toward Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 質頓兵不肯時發，又顧戀嬖妾，棄軍營壘，單馬還城，散用台庫見錢六七百萬，為有司所糾，上不問。

translations.literal: Zhi halted his troops and would not advance on schedule; again he doted on a favorite concubine, abandoned the army camps and ramparts, returned to the city alone on one horse, and scattered six or seven million in ready cash from the treasury — impeached by the responsible offices; the Emperor did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi halted his troops and would not advance on schedule; again he doted on a favorite concubine, abandoned the army camps and ramparts, returned to the city alone on one horse, and scattered six or seven million in ready cash from the treasury — impeached by the responsible offices; the emperor did not inquire.

sentences.zh: 元凶弑立，以質為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince usurped and succeeded he made Zhi Magistrate of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince usurped and succeeded he made Zhi magistrate of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 質家遣門生師顗報質，具言文帝崩問。

translations.literal: Zhi's household sent his student Shi Yan to report to Zhi, fully stating Emperor Wen's death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's household sent his student Shi Yan to report to Zhi, fully stating Emperor Wen's death.

sentences.zh: 質使告司空義宣及孝武帝，而自率眾五千馳下討逆，自陽口進江陵見義宣。

translations.literal: Zhi had Yan inform Minister of Works Yixuan and Emperor Xiaowu, and himself led five thousand men racing down to suppress the usurper; from Yangkou he advanced to Jiangling to see Yixuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had Yan inform minister of works Yixuan and Emperor Xiaowu, and himself led five thousand men racing down to suppress the usurper; from Yangkou he advanced to Jiangling to see Yixuan.

sentences.zh: 時質諸子在都，聞質舉義，並逃亡。

translations.literal: At that time Zhi's sons were all in the capital; hearing Zhi had raised righteousness they all fled.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhi's sons were all in the capital; hearing Zhi had raised righteousness they all fled.

sentences.zh: 義宣始得質報，即日舉兵馳信報孝武，板進質號征北將軍。

translations.literal: When Yixuan first received Zhi's report he that day raised troops and sent urgent word to Xiaowu; by provisional appointment Zhi was promoted General Who Pacifies the North.
